ITQAN:v4p431/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p431/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p431/r10.claim: The only adjacent kāf-kāf sequences without an intervening letter occur in “manāsikakum” and “mā salakakum.”
ITQAN:v4p431/r10.anchor: ولا كافان كذلك إلا ﴿ مناسككم ﴾ ﴿ ما سلككم ﴾

DAMGHANI:v1p180/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r2.claim: Dhikr can mean verbal remembrance or mention.
DAMGHANI:v1p180/r2.anchor: الثاني : الذكر باللسان قوله تعالى في سورة النساء

SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r1.claim: مناسك is the plural of منسك, with either fatḥa or kasra on its second sīn; its derivation was treated shortly before.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r1.anchor: جمع " منسك " بفتح السين وكسرها، وسيأتي تحقيقهما

SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r2.claim: The readers generally pronounce the form distinctly; Abū ʿAmr is reported to assimilate it by treating the inflectional vowel like a building vowel and deleting it. The assimilation occurs here unlike in جباههم and وجوههم.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r2.anchor: وروى عن أبي عمرو الإدغام، قالوا: شبه الإعراب بحركة البناء فحذفها للإدغام

SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r3.claim: The comparison kāf works as in كما هداكم, except that the earlier discussion also considered whether it means على or لام.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r3.anchor: إلا في كونها بمعنى " على " أو بمعنى اللام، فليلتفت إليه

SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r4.claim: The majority read آباءكم in the accusative as object of the verbal noun, which is annexed to its agent in the regular construction.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r4.anchor: والجمهور على نصب " آباءكم " مفعولا به، والمصدر مضاف لفاعله

SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r5.claim: Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb reads آباؤكم in the nominative, construing the verbal noun as annexed to its object: a son avidly remembers his father.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r5.anchor: وقرأ محمد بن كعب: " آباؤكم " رفعا، على أن المصدر مضاف للمفعول

SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r6.claim: A second reading attributed to Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb has the singular أباكم for the generic father; it follows the majority's agent-annexed construction. Nominative case by a dialect treating أباك like a shortened noun is considered remote.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200/r6.anchor: وروي عنه أيضا: " أباكم " بالإفراد على إرادة الجنس، وهي توافق قراءة الجماعة

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r1.claim: One genitive parse coordinates أشد with the genitive ذكركم under the comparison kāf, estimating like a more intense remembrance; it figuratively makes remembrance itself remember. Abū al-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya follow it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r1.anchor: وإليه ذهب الزجاج، وتبعه أبو البقاء، وابن عطية

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r2.claim: Another genitive parse coordinates أشد with the genitive pronoun in ذكركم: more intense remembrance by you. Its meaning avoids personifying remembrance, but Basran grammarians prohibit coordination on a genitive pronoun without repeating the preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r2.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله الزمخشري معنى حسن، ليس فيه تجوز بأن يجعل للذكر ذكر

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r3.claim: An accusative parse coordinates أشد with آباءكم, estimating people more intense in remembrance than your fathers; ذكرا is their distinguishing measure, so remembrance is not personified.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r3.anchor: أن يكون معطوفا على " آباءكم " قال الزمخشري

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r4.speaker: أبو علي
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī and Ibn Jinnī coordinate أشد with the syntactic position of the kāf, understood as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun; this figuratively treats remembrance as a rememberer.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r4.anchor: وهذا تخريج أبي علي وابن جني

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r5.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r5.claim: Makkī supplies an implicit verb: remember Him with remembrance more intense than your remembrance of your fathers; the verbal noun is an accusative circumstantial description.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#2/r5.anchor: الثالث: قاله مكي: أن يكون منصوبا بإضمار فعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r1.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ supplies an implicit be: be more intense in remembering God than you are in remembering your fathers, which he considers easier than the figurative parse.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r1.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " وعندي أن الكلام محمول على المعنى، والتقدير

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r2.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r2.claim: A fifth accusative parse makes أشد a circumstantial modifier of ذكرا, as though it were a delayed adjective; the Shaykh illustrates fronted adjective becoming circumstantial with a line about a desolate trace of Laylā.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r2.anchor: الخامس: أن يكون " أشد " نصبا على الحال من " ذكرا "

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r3.claim: The Shaykh says the direct sense is to remember God with remembrance matching or surpassing remembrance of fathers; the five preceding parses are all weak.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r3.anchor: قاله الشيخ، فإنه قال بعد ذكره ثلاثة أوجه لنصبه ووجهين لجره

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r4.claim: For the preferred reading, ذكرا may coordinate with the syntactic position of the kāf, though أو is separated from its conjunct by circumstantial أشد. Grammarians permit separation only when the conjunction exceeds one letter and the intervening word is an oath, adverb, or prepositional phrase; the Shaykh treats the circumstance as estimated with a preposition, like an adverb.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r4.anchor: قاله الشيخ، فإنه قال بعد ذكره ثلاثة أوجه لنصبه ووجهين لجره

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r5.claim: Alternatively, ذكرا is the verbal noun governed by فاذكروا; كذكركم is a fronted circumstance originally adjectival to it, and أشد coordinates with that circumstance.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#3/r5.anchor: قاله الشيخ، فإنه قال بعد ذكره ثلاثة أوجه لنصبه ووجهين لجره

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#4/r1.claim: The usual analysis makes ذكرا a specification of degree, but the accusative is puzzling because remembrance is the same kind as the comparison term and would normally be genitive. Earlier parses resolve this by personifying remembrance, making أشد describe persons or a circumstance, or supplying a verb.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#4/r1.anchor: و " ذكرا " تمييز عند غير الشيخ كما تقدم، واستشكلوا كونه تمييزا منصوبا

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#4/r2.claim: One analysis takes أو as permissive, allowing either way of remembering.

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#4/r3.claim: Another analysis takes أو as a choice between alternatives.

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#4/r4.claim: A third analysis takes أو in the sense of بل, rather.

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r1.claim: The strongest parse makes من the subject, with its predicate in the preceding prepositional phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r1.anchor: " من " مبتدأ، وخبره في الجار قبله

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r2.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash allows من to function as an agent.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون فاعلة عند الأخفش

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r3.claim: A further analysis treats من as an indefinite noun modified by a descriptive clause.

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r4.claim: The phrasing shifts from the preceding pattern: it would have said among you, but من is treated by meaning as plural in our Lord, grant us; agreement with its singular form would be Lord, grant me.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r4.anchor: وفي هذا الكلام التفات، إذ لو جرى على النسق الأول لقيل

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r5.claim: The second object of آتنا is most clearly omitted for concision or left general: grant us what we want or our request.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r5.anchor: أظهرها: أنه محذوف اختصارا أو اقتصارا،

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r6.claim: One alternative makes في mean من, yielding grant us from the world; the author rejects it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r6.anchor: والثاني: أن " في " بمعنى " من " أي: من الدنيا

SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r7.claim: Another alternative treats في as an extra particle, yielding grant us the world; the author rejects it too.
SAMIN-DURR:2:200#5/r7.anchor: والثالث: أنها زائدة، أي: آتنا الدنيا، وليسا بشيء

ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r1.claim: Manāsik are the acts of worship commanded during pilgrimage.
ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r1.anchor: أي متعبداتكم التي أمرتم بها في الحج

ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r2.claim: After completing the rites, Arabs stood between the mosque at Minā and the mountain, listing their fathers’ virtues and recalling their notable days.
ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r2.anchor: وكانت العرب إذا قضت مناسكها، وقفت بين المسجد بمنى وبين الجبل فتعدد فضائل آبائها

ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r3.claim: God redirects that remembrance to Himself and calls for more: declare His oneness and recount His blessings, since blessings attributed to ancestors come from God and merit thanks to Him.
ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r3.anchor: وأن يزيدوا على ذلك الذكر فيذكروا الله بتوحيده وتعديد نعمه

ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r4.claim: Ashadda is in a genitive syntactic position but indeclinable on the afʿal pattern as an adjective; alternatively it is accusative under an understood ‘remember Him more intensely.’
ZAJJAJ:v1p273#2/r4.anchor: (أشد) في موضع خفض ولكنه لا يتصرف لأنه على مثال أفعل، وهو صفته، وإن شئت كان نصبا

ZAJJAJ:v1p274/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p274/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p274/r1.claim: Ātinā is a pause point because it is a supplication; it means ‘give us in this world.’
ZAJJAJ:v1p274/r1.anchor: (آتنا) وقف لأنه دعاء، ومعناه أعطنا في الدنيا

ZAJJAJ:v1p274/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p274/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p274/r2.claim: These are Arab polytheists who asked for worldly ease but sought no afterlife share because they did not believe in it.
ZAJJAJ:v1p274/r2.anchor: وهؤلاء مشركو العرب كانوا يسألون التوسعة عليهم في الدنيا ولا يسألون حظا من الآخرة

ZAJJAJ:v1p274/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p274/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p274/r3.claim: Khalāq means an abundant share of good.
ZAJJAJ:v1p274/r3.anchor: يعني هؤلاء، والخلاق النصيب الوافر من الخير.

ASAD-NOTES:2:200#n185/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:200#n185/r1.speaker: Most of the commentators
ASAD-NOTES:2:200#n185/r1.claim: Most commentators take the comparison to fathers as referring to pre-Islamic Arabs’ custom of praising their ancestors’ greatness and supposed virtues at gatherings.
ASAD-NOTES:2:200#n185/r1.anchor: Most of the commentators see in this passage a reference to the custom of the pre-Islamic Arabs to extol

ASAD-NOTES:2:200#n185/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:200#n185/r2.speaker: Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi and Abu Muslim
ASAD-NOTES:2:200#n185/r2.claim: These early scholars instead understand the words as referring to actual fathers or, by implication, both parents, whom children regard as embodiments of goodness and power.
ASAD-NOTES:2:200#n185/r2.anchor: e.g., Ad-Dahhak, Ar-Rabi and Abu Muslim - are of the opinion that what is meant here are actual fathers

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p401/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p401/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p401/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses khalaq as a share; Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt's line about having no share supports the sense, which occurs in the cited verses.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p401/r4.anchor: وسأل ابن الأزرق عن قوله تعالى: {خَلَاقٍ} فقال ابن عباس: نصيب. وشاهده قول أمية

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p79#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p79#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p79#2/r1.claim: Qatada says pilgrims used to gather after the rites to boast and recount their forebears and their exploits; they were told to replace this with remembrance of God, just as much or more.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p79#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ كذكركم آباءكم ﴾ قال إذا قضوا مناسكهم اجتمعوا فافتخروا وذكروا آباءهم وأيامها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r2.claim: One reported occasion of revelation is that pilgrims gathered and boasted about their fathers' generosity, fighting, feasting, camel sacrifice, freeing captives, and other deeds; the verse redirected their remembrance to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r2.anchor: وسبب نزولها أنهم كانوا إذا اجتمعوا في الموسم تفاخروا بآبائهم، فيقول أحدهم: كان يقري الضيف، ويضرب بالسيف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says people used to swear by their fathers when speaking, saying, for example, By my father; the verse was revealed in response.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: كانوا إذا حدثوا أقسموا بالآباء، فيقولون. وأبيك، فنزلت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r4.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says that at Mina after the rites, a man would ask God to grant him wealth like his father's, praising the father rather than mentioning God; Abu Wa'il and Ibn Zayd give this as the verse's meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: كانوا إذا قضوا المناسك وأقاموا بمنى يقوم الرجل ويسأل الله فيقول: اللهم إن أبي كان عظيم الجفنة، كثير المال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r5.claim: Here قضى means to perform, finish, and complete the rites, as in the phrase فإذا قضيت الصلاة; when an act is attributed to the person doing it, قضى means completion, whereas doing it on another's behalf can mean imposing or adjudicating it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r5.anchor: فإذا قضيتم، أي أديتم وفرغتم. كقوله: فإذا قضيت الصلاة أي: أديت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r6.claim: Although قضاء can also refer to performing missed worship outside its appointed time, that is not the meaning here; when the act is one's own, the word indicates completion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r6.anchor: وقد يعبر بالقضاء عن ما يفعل من العبادات خارج الوقت المحدود، والقضاء إذا علق على فعل النفس فالمراد منه الإتمام والفراغ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r7.claim: Some exegetes take the condition to mean beginning rather than finishing Hajj, and understand remembrance as the supplications at Arafat and the Mashʿar and the rites of circumambulation and saʿy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r7.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين: يحتمل أن يكون هذا الشرط والجزاء، كقولك: إذا حججت فطف وقف بعرفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects the beginning-of-Hajj reading as contrary to the apparent meaning of completion, supported by the فاء after the preceding clauses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r8.anchor: وهذا خلاف الظاهر، لأن الظاهر الفراغ من المناسك لا الشروع فيها، ويؤيد ذلك مجيء الفاء في: فإذا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r9.claim: Manasik can mean the places of worship, requiring an omitted noun for their acts; it can mean the worship acts themselves, attributed to al-Hasan, or sacrifices and bloodletting, attributed to Mujahid.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p305/r9.anchor: والمناسك هي مواضع العبادة، فيكون هذا على حذف مضاف، أي: أعمال مناسككم، أو العبادات نفسها المأمور بها في الحج، قاله الحسن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r1.claim: After completing the standing at Arafat and leaving Mina, magnify and praise God for guiding and easing the difficult rites until the duty is fulfilled.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r1.anchor: إذا فرغتم من الوقوف بعرفة، ونفرتم من منى، فعظموا الله وأثنوا عليه إذ هداكم لهذه الطاعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r2.claim: One reported interpretation takes the remembrance as invoking God over the sacrificial animal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r2.anchor: الذكر هنا هو ذكر الله على الذبيحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r3.claim: Another interpretation identifies the remembrance as the takbirs after prayer on the Sacrifice day and the days of Tashriq.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r3.anchor: هو التكبيرات بعد الصلاة في يوم النحر وأيام التشريق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r4.claim: The command redirects people from mentioning their fathers to remembering God as intensely as they formerly recalled their fathers' boasts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r4.anchor: المقصود تحويلهم عن ذكر آبائهم إلى ذكره تعالى كذكركم آباءكم تقدم هذا هو ذكر مفاخرهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r5.claim: A further reported sense is asking God to grant them what He granted their forefathers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r5.anchor: السؤال من الله أن يعطيهم مثل ما أعطى آباءهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r6.claim: Another reported explanation takes the phrase as swearing by their fathers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r6.anchor: أو القسم بآبائهم، وقيل: ذكر آباءهم في حال الصغر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r7.claim: One interpretation recalls a child's early speech, repeatedly calling for his father as he first learns to speak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r7.anchor: ذكر آباءهم في حال الصغر، ولهجه بأبيه يقول: أبة أبة، أول ما يتكلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r8.claim: Abu al-Jawza reports from Ibn Abbas that remembrance means becoming angry for God as one becomes angry when one's parents are insulted.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r8.anchor: الغضب لله كما تغضب لوالديك إذا سبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r9.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya transmits Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi's reading with آباؤكم nominative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r9.anchor: أن محمد بن كعب القرظي قرأ:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r10.claim: On the nominative reading, آباؤكم is the subject of the verbal noun, annexed to its object: your fathers remember you.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r10.anchor: ووجه الرفع أنه فاعل بالمصدر، والمصدر مضاف إلى المفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r11.claim: That reading urges people to invoke God as devotedly as a person constantly mentions his child.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r11.anchor: ابتهلوا بذكر الله والهجوا به كما يلهج المرء بذكر ابنه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r12.speaker: محمد بن كعب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r12.claim: Other transmitters report Muhammad ibn Ka'b reading أباكم in the singular; the plural audience makes the collective sense clear.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r12.anchor: ونقل غيره عن محمد بن كعب أنه قرأ: أباكم، على الإفراد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r13.claim: Commentators proposed several parses because they assumed ذكرًا must be an accusative specification after the comparative, although a same-kind comparison normally takes the genitive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r13.anchor: جوزوا في إعرابه وجوها اضطروا إليها لاعتقادهم أن ذكرا بعد أشد تمييزا بعد أفعل التفضيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r14.claim: One view takes أو as offering a choice between two alternatives.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r15.claim: Another view takes أو to indicate permission.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r16.claim: A third view reads أو as بل, meaning rather or even more intensely.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p306/r16.anchor: وقيل: بمعنى بل أشد، جوزوا في إعرابه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r1.speaker: أبو علي وابن جني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r1.claim: Abu Ali and Ibn Jinni coordinate ذكرا to the syntactic position of the كاف, treating it as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun; this makes remembrance figuratively have a remembrance.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari coordinates أشد with آبائكم, estimating people more intense in remembrance than your fathers, with ذكرًا describing those people's action.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r2.anchor: الثاني: أن يكون معطوفا على آبائكم، قاله الزمخشري، قال: بمعنى أو أشد ذكرا من آبائكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan calls al-Zamakhshari's parse awkward: it yields people more intense than the fathers in your remembrance of them, while the remembrance is performed by those people.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r4.claim: A third parse supplies an implicit verb of being: be more intense in remembering God than in remembering your fathers; the command to remember supports this sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r4.anchor: أنه منصوب بإضمار فعل الكون. والكلام محمول على المعنى.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa calls the implicit-verb parse easier than making remembrance itself figuratively have remembrance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r5.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: قال: وهذا أسهل من حمله على المجاز،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r6.speaker: الزجاج وابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj, Ibn Atiyya, and others allow genitive أشد coordinated with ذكركم, yielding a remembrance like a more intense remembrance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r6.anchor: أن يكون معطوفا على: ذكركم، الزجاج، وابن عطية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows genitive أشد coordinated with the pronoun governed by the verbal noun, without repeating the preposition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r7.anchor: الثاني: أن يكون معطوفا على الضمير المجرور بالمصدر في: كذكركم، قاله الزمخشري.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r8.claim: Abu Hayyan judges all five proposed parses weak and says the Qur'an should be kept clear of them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r8.anchor: فهي خمسة وجوه من الإعراب كلها ضعيف، والذي يتبادر إليه الذهن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r9.claim: The immediate sense is to remember God with remembrance equal to or stronger than the remembrance people give their fathers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r9.anchor: والذي يتبادر إليه الذهن في الآية أنهم أمروا بأن يذكروا الله ذكرا يماثل ذكر آبائهم أو أشد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p307/r10.claim: Abu Hayyan parses أشد as an accusative circumstantial modifier of ذكرًا, equivalent to delayed ذكرا أشد من ذكركم آباءكم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r1.claim: He compares the fronted circumstantial construction to the poetic wording لمية موحشا طلل, whose regular order would be لمية طلل موحش.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r1.anchor: لمية موحشا طلل فلو تأخر لكان: لمية طلل موحش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r2.claim: He also allows ذكرا as a verbal noun from فاذكروا, with أشد coordinated to the syntactic position of كاف as a circumstantial modifier.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ذكرا مصدرا، لقوله: فاذكروا كذكركم، في موضع الحال،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r3.claim: The delayed wording makes a fitting cadence and avoids repeating ذكر in فاذكروا ذكرا كذكركم; this explains why the phrase comes late.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r3.anchor: وحسن تأخره أنه كالفاصلة في جنس المقطع. ولو تقدم لكان: فاذكروا ذكرا كذكركم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r4.claim: The objection that أو separates a conjunction from its coordinated word fails: an intervening circumstantial modifier is semantically like an adverbial and can be treated similarly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r4.anchor: لا يقال في الوجه الأول: أنه يلزم فيه الفصل بين حرف العطف وهو: أو، وبين المعطوف الذي هو: ذكرا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan favors the circumstantial parse over strained analyses that make ذكرًا a specification after the comparative and force figurative readings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r5.anchor: وهذا أولى من جعل: ذكرا، تمييزا لأفعل التفضيل الذي هو وصف في المعنى،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r6.claim: Some commentators say the verse contrasts those remembering God before the Prophet's mission with believers after it, who know reward and punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r6.anchor: حال الذاكرين له قبل مبعثه، وحال المؤمنين بعد مبعثه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan instead sees a division among pilgrims commanded to remember God: some ask only for worldly goods, while others ask for good in this life and the next.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p308/r7.anchor: ينقسمون في السؤال إلى من يغلب عليه حب الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r1.claim: The shift to third person excludes worldly-only petitioners from the direct address, since limiting prayer to this life is unworthy of a rational addressee.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r1.anchor: وحكمة هذا الالتفات أنهم ما وجهوا بهذا الذي لا ينبغي أن يسلكه عاقل، وهو الاقتصار على الدنيا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r2.claim: This is an elegant exhaustive division into two groups; Abu Hayyan rejects the Sufis' proposed third group, people content with God's decree who make no supplication.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r2.anchor: وهذا من التقسيم الذي هو من جملة ضروب البيان، وهو تقسيم بديع يحصره المقسم إلى هذين النوعين، لا على ما يذهب إليه الصوفية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r3.claim: The second object of آتنا is omitted; possible estimates include what you wish to grant or our request.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r3.anchor: ومفعول آتنا الثاني محذوف، تقديره: ما تريد، أو: مطلوبنا، أو ما أشبه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r4.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects treating في as redundant and الدنيا as the second object, or changing في to mean من and omitting both objects; only one object may be omitted with this verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r4.anchor: هذا وجعل في زائدة، وتكون الدنيا المفعول الثاني قول ساقط، وكذلك جعل في بمعنى: من، حتى يكون في موضع المفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r5.claim: The clause can mean that the worldly-only petitioner has no afterlife share because he sought only this world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r5.anchor: لا نصيب له في الآخرة لاقتصاره على الدنيا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r6.claim: Alternatively, it says the petitioner has no desire to seek an afterlife share, reinforcing his exclusive worldly request.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r6.anchor: إخبارا عن الداعي بأنه ما له في الآخرة من طلب نصيب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan points back to his explanation of the same phrase in the discussion of 2:102.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r7.anchor: تقدم تفسير هذا في قوله: ولقد علموا لمن اشتراه ما له في الآخرة من خلاق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r8.claim: Although من is singular, the petition is plural because many people seek only worldly aims; singular wording might suggest few do so.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r8.anchor: وجمع في قوله: ربنا آتنا في الدنيا ولو جرى على لفظ من، لكان: رب آتني.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r9.claim: حسنة is unrestricted: the petitioners ask God for a good condition in this world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r9.anchor: الحسنة: مطلقة، والمعنى: أنهم سألوا الله في الدنيا الحالة الحسنة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r10.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r10.claim: Ali interprets worldly good as a righteous wife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r10.anchor: المرأة الصالحة، قاله علي. أو: العافية في الصحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r11.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r11.claim: Qatada interprets worldly good as health and enough money.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r11.anchor: العافية في الصحة وكفاف المال، قاله قتادة. أو: العلم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r12.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r12.claim: Al-Hasan interprets worldly good as knowledge or worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r12.anchor: أو: العلم، أو العبادة، قاله الحسن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r13.speaker: السدي وأبو وائل وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r13.claim: Al-Suddi, Abu Wa'il, and Ibn Zayd interpret worldly good as wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r13.anchor: المال، قاله السدي، وأبو وائل، وابن زيد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r14.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r14.claim: Muqatil interprets it as abundant provision.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r15.speaker: ابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r15.claim: Ibn Qutayba interprets it as blessing in this world.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r15.anchor: النعمة في الدنيا، قاله: ابن قتيبة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r16.claim: Other suggested senses are contentment with provision, success and protection from error, or righteous children.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p309/r16.anchor: القناعة بالرزق، أو: التوفيق والعصمة، أو: الأولاد الأبرار،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p314/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p314/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p314/r11.claim: After the command to seek forgiveness, the passage commands remembrance after completing the rites.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p314/r11.anchor: ثم أمر بالاستغفار، ثم أمر بعد أداء المناسك بذكر الله تعالى،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p314/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p314/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p314/r12.claim: People treated recalling and praising their fathers' noble deeds as the height of remembrance; God uses that familiar intensity as a comparison and commands even more remembrance so they never forget Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p314/r12.anchor: كان الإنسان كثيرا ما يذكر أباه ويثني عليه بما أسلفه من كريم المآثر، وكان ذلك عندهم الغاية في الذكر، مثل ذكر الله بذلك الذكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p314#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p314#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p314#2/r1.claim: Pilgrims' aims divide into those seeking only this world and those seeking worldly and afterlife good; the first group has no afterlife share.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p314#2/r1.anchor: قسم مقصد الحاج إلى دنيوي صرف، وإلى دنيوي وأخروي، وبين ذلك في سؤاله إياه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r1.claim: Once you have performed and finished the rites of pilgrimage, remember God as you used to remember your fathers after the pilgrimage, boasting of their deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r1.anchor: أي أديتم عباداتكم الحجية وفرغتم منها فأذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r2.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that in pre-Islamic times people sat after pilgrimage all day recalling their fathers’ deeds and lineage; the verse redirected this remembrance to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r2.anchor: كان أهل الجاهلية يجلسون بعد الحج فيذكرون أيام آبائهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r3.claim: One parsing makes “stronger remembrance” genitive with “remembrance,” treating remembrance as an agent by metaphor: remember God as you remember your fathers or more intensely.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r3.anchor: مجرور معطوف على الذكر بجعل الذكر ذاكرا على المجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, “stronger” coordinates with the genitive pronoun under the permissive Kūfan analysis, meaning remembrance of people whose remembrance exceeds yours.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r4.anchor: على ما أضيف إليه بناءا على مذهب الكوفيين المجوزين للعطف على الضمير المجرور

ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r5.claim: An accusative parsing coordinates “stronger” with “your fathers,” taking “remembrance” passively: God is more remembered than your fathers.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r5.anchor: منصوب بالعطف على ( آباءكم ) و ( ذكرا ) من فعل المبني للمفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r6.claim: An ellipsis may instead mean: let your remembrance of God be stronger than your remembrance of your fathers.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r6.anchor: أي ليكن ذكركم الله تعالى أشد من ذكركم آباءكم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r7.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r7.claim: Al-Baḥr prefers taking “stronger” as a circumstantial accusative modifying “remembrance”; delaying “remembrance” gives the verse its cadence and avoids awkward repetition.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r7.anchor: في البحر أن يكون ( أشد ) نصب على الحال من ذكرا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r8.claim: The circumstantial parse is challenged: “or stronger” without “remembrance” would be expected, since the desired object is remembrance characterized as stronger, not remembering while in a stronger state.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p89#2/r8.anchor: على هذا الوجه أن يقال أو أشد بدون ( ذكرا )

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r1.claim: Completing the rites means finishing the pilgrimage and slaughtering the sacrificial animals, after stoning Jamrat al-ʿAqaba and settling in Minā.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r1.anchor: {فإذا قضيتم مناسككم} أي فرغتم من حجكم وذبحتم نسائككم، أي ذبائحكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r2.claim: Nusuk here means sacrifice: nasaka is used when a person slaughters his sacrificial animal.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r2.anchor: يقال: نسك الرجل ينسك نسكا إذا ذبح نسيكته

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r3.claim: Remember God through takbīr, praise, and extolling Him; Arabs had stood at the House after pilgrimage to boast about their ancestors, so God tells them to remember Him, since He favored them and their forebears.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r3.anchor: فاذكروا الله} بالتكبير والتحميد والثناء عليه {كذكركم آباءكم} وذلك أن العرب كانت إذا فرغت من الحج

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿAṭāʾ interpret the comparison as remembering God as small children remember their fathers, since a child’s first speech dwells on his father; remember God alone or more intensely.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس وعطاء: معناه فاذكروا الله كذكر الصبيان الصغار الآباء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r5.claim: Asked how a person might go a whole day without mentioning his father, Ibn ʿAbbās says one should be more angered when God is disobeyed than when one’s parents are insulted.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ليس كذلك ولكن أن تغضب لله إذا عصي أشد من غضبك لوالديك إذا شتما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r6.claim: The phrase means more intense, or rather more frequent, remembrance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r6.anchor: أو أشد ذكرا} يعني: وأشد ذكرا، وبل أشد، أي وأكثر ذكرا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r7.claim: The people asking only for worldly goods are polytheists who prayed for livestock and servants; a man might appeal to his father’s former wealth and ask to receive the same.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r7.anchor: أراد به المشركين كانوا لا يسألون الله تعالى في الحج إلا الدنيا يقولون اللهم أعطنا غنما وإبلا وبقرا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r8.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r8.claim: Qatāda calls this a servant whose intention is worldly life, for whose sake he spends, works, and exerts himself; he has no portion in the hereafter.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p231/r8.anchor: قال قتادة هذا عبد نيته الدنيا لها أنفق ولها عمل ونصب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r1.claim: After completing the rites and devotional acts of Hajj, worshippers are to remember God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r1.anchor: فإذا قضيتم العبادات الحجية وفرغتم منها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r2.claim: They should remember God abundantly, as they used to mention their fathers while boasting.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r2.anchor: فاكثروا ذكره وبالغوا فيه كما تفعلون بذكر آبائكم في المفاخرة.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r3.claim: After Hajj the Arabs used to stand at Minā between the mosque and mountain, recounting their ancestors’ glories and past merits.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r3.anchor: وكانت العرب إذا قضوا مناسكهم وقفوا بمنى بين المسجد والجبل

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r4.claim: One parsing makes “stronger remembrance” genitive coordinated with dhikr, metaphorically treating remembrance as the one who remembers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r4.anchor: إما مجرور معطوف على الذكر يجعل الذكر ذاكرا على المجاز

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r5.claim: A weaker alternative coordinates the phrase with its genitive complement, meaning remembrance like that of people more intense than you.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r5.anchor: أو على ما أضيف إليه على ضعف بمعنى أو كذكر قوم أشد منكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r6.claim: Another parsing puts “stronger” in the accusative coordinated with “your fathers,” meaning more mentioned than your fathers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r6.anchor: بالعطف على آباءكم وذكرا من فعل المذكور بمعنى أو كذكركم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r7.claim: An implied command may instead mean: be more intense in remembering God than you are in remembering your fathers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r7.anchor: أم بمضمر دل عليه المعنى تقديره: أو كونوا أشد ذكرا لله

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r8.claim: Worshippers divide into those who seek only worldly gain through remembrance and those who seek good in both abodes; the verse urges abundant remembrance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r8.anchor: تفصيل للذاكرين إلى مقل لا يطلب بذكر الله تعالى إلا الدنيا

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r9.claim: The worldly petitioner asks God to make His gift and grant theirs in this life.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r10.claim: Khalaq means a share or portion; such a petitioner has none in the Hereafter because his concern is confined to worldly life.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r10.anchor: أي نصيب وحظ لأن همه مقصور بالدنيا،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r11.claim: A second explanation takes khalaq as a sought share or allotment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:200/r11.anchor: لأن همه مقصور بالدنيا، أو من طلب خلاق.

BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r1.claim: After completing the acts of worship prescribed for Hajj, believers should devote themselves to remembering God.
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r1.anchor: أتممتم عباداتكم التي أمرتم بها في الحج وفرغتم منها

BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r2.claim: At Minā, Arabs used to recall their ancestors' boasts and glorious days to gain fame and status; God forbade that habit and ordered His own praise and remembrance in its place.
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r2.anchor: وكانت العرب إذا قضوا مناسكهم وقفوا بمنى بين المسجد والجبل

BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r3.claim: God alone is the source of all good; ancestors are His servants and obtained their achievements through His grace, so His praise should replace boasting about them.
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r3.anchor: إذ الخير كله من عنده وآباؤهم عبيده ونالوا ما نالوا بأفضاله

BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r4.speaker: السعدي
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r4.claim: Saʿdī's couplet says that good comes from God through divine enabling, not from one servant independently reaching another.
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r4.anchor: قال السعدي قدس سره : كراز حق نه توفيق خيري رسد

BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r5.claim: The phrase can mean remembering God as much as one remembered ancestors, or with even more intense remembrance; the genitive coordination figuratively treats remembrance as a rememberer.
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r5.anchor: مجرور معطوف على الذكر بجعله ذاكرا على المجاز أي : اذكروه

BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r6.claim: An adjective in an annexed construction normally shares the preceding noun's category, while an accusative complement can differ; here the annexation is justified by personifying remembrance as remembering another remembrance.
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r6.anchor: أفعل إنما يضاف إلى ما بعده إذا كان من جنس ما قبله

BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r7.claim: Attributing remembrance to remembrance is possible figuratively when one hears a mention and thereby remembers, so the first remembrance seems to have remembered.
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r7.anchor: ويجوز نسبة الذكر إلى الذكر بأن يسمع إنسان الذكر فيذكر

BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r8.claim: Those who ask only for worldly gifts such as status, wealth, and victory are polytheists, whose Hajj supplication seeks only immediate worldly advantage.
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r8.anchor: في ذكره مقتصرا على طلب الدنيا

BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r9.claim: Because such a person's concern is confined to this world, he has no share in the Hereafter: at the holiest standing he asked for the lowest goods and neglected lasting bliss.
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r9.anchor: همه مقصور على الدنيا حيث سأل في أعز المواقف أحقر المطالب

BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p261#2/r10.claim: The other pilgrims ask for the good of both abodes, including health, sufficiency, and enabling grace to do good.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p378/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p378/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p378/r11.claim: Because people tend to relax and stop remembering after completing worship, and Arabs then recited their ancestors' boasts, the command redirects remembrance to God after the rites.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p378/r11.anchor: ولما أمرهم بالذكر في المناسك وكان الإنسان فيها بصدد الذكر أمرهم بالذكر بعد قضائها لأن من فرغ من العبادة كان بصدد أن يستريح

BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r1.claim: Though parents raised them, that upbringing ultimately comes from God; parents also exposed them to trials and misled them, while God is the ultimate source of their blessings and guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r1.anchor: لكونهم أحسنوا إليكم بالتربية التي هي في الحقيقة من فضل الله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r2.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r2.claim: The change from the familiar formula of speech accompanies the change from the familiar pilgrimage station, breaking people of their accustomed practices and states.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r2.anchor: قال الحرالي : فانتظم ذكر إخراجهم عن قولهم المعهود بإخراجهم عن موقفهم المعهود

BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r3.claim: Harali warns that people may treat God like an honored human because they are attached to what they see and have weak faith in what they hear or know.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r3.anchor: وذلك عن بلية ما غلب عليهم من التقيد بما يرون وضعف الإيمان بما سمعوا أو علموا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r4.claim: The author cites the saying, Be ashamed before God as you would be ashamed before a dignified man among your people, as an analogy for the commanded reverence.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r4.anchor: استحي من الله كما تستحيي رجلا جليلا من قومك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r5.claim: Remember God even more intensely because His beneficence is universal; shun associating a partner with Him at least as strongly as a son would reject a partner for his father.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r5.anchor: أي اذكروا الله ذكرا أعلى من ذلك بأن تذكروه ذكرا أشد من ذكركم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r6.claim: Harali says the command raises the discourse to what is more fitting for God: preferring what pertains to Him over what pertains to creatures.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r6.anchor: قال الحرالي : فرفع الخطاب إلى ما هو أ ليق بالحق من إيثار ما يرجع إليه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r7.claim: After commanding remembrance and exclusive devotion to God, the verse divides people according to whether they accept that command.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r7.anchor: سبب عنه تقسيم الناس في قبول الأمر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r8.claim: The first group has the world as its chief concern and asks only for worldly benefit, with no afterlife share because its members neither desire nor strive for it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r8.anchor: تكون الدنيا أكبر همه فلا التفات له إلى غيرها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r9.claim: The singular pronoun with man follows the word's singular grammatical form; the author takes this as glad tidings that few in this community will be lost.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r9.anchor: أفرد الضمير رعاية للفظ من بشارة بأن الهالك في هذه الأمة إن شاء الله قليل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r10.claim: One analysis leaves the object of the worldly request unstated, meaning whatever the supplicant wants.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r11.claim: Alternatively, the expression may coordinate with an implied clause meaning God gives whatever He chooses, not necessarily what the supplicant requested.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r11.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون عطفا على ما تقديره : فيعطيه ما شاء سبحانه منها لا ما طلب هو

BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r12.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r12.claim: Harali defines khalaq as a share suited to a person's created nature and character.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p379/r12.anchor: قال الحرالي : والخلاق الحظ اللائق بالخلق والخلق

DURR-FULL:v1p556/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas advises companions, male or female, not to fast on Arafah, a day of eating, drinking, and takbir.
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقول: من يصحبني منكم من ذكر أو أنثى فلا يصومن يوم عرفة

DURR-FULL:v1p556/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r2.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r2.claim: Ata glosses completing the rites as completing Hajj.
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r2.anchor: عن عطاء {فإذا قضيتم مناسككم} قال: حجكم

DURR-FULL:v1p556/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r3.claim: Mujahid also glosses the rites as Hajj.
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {فإذا قضيتم مناسككم} قال: حجكم

DURR-FULL:v1p556/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r4.claim: Mujahid identifies the rites with slaughtering sacrifice; Arabs boasted of ancestors on the Day of Sacrifice, and were told to remember God instead.
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {فإذا قضيتم مناسككم} قال: اهراقه الدماء {فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم}

DURR-FULL:v1p556/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says polytheists spent Hajj recalling ancestors' days and lineages, prompting the command to remember God as much or more.
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان المشركون يجلسون في الحج فيذكرون فيه أيام آبائهم

DURR-FULL:v1p556/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says pre-Islamic pilgrims listed fathers' generosity, carrying loads, and paying bloodwits, with no remembrance beyond their deeds.
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان أهل الجاهلية يقفون في الموسم يقول الرجل منهم: كان أبي يطعم

DURR-FULL:v1p556/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r7.speaker: عبد اله بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r7.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says people boasted of their forefathers after finishing Hajj, and the verse was revealed in response.
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r7.anchor: عن عبد اله بن الزبير قال: كانوا إذا فزعوا من حجهم تفاخروا بالآباء

DURR-FULL:v1p556/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r8.claim: Mujahid says pilgrims at the Jamara recalled their fathers and pre-Islamic deeds after completing rites, occasioning the verse.
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: كانوا إذا قضوا مناسكهم وقفوا عند الجمرة فذكروا آباءهم

DURR-FULL:v1p556/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r9.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r9.claim: Anas reports that pre-Islamic pilgrims recalled their fathers' deeds, such as feeding people.
DURR-FULL:v1p556/r9.anchor: عن أنس قال: كانوا في الجاهلية يذكرون آباءهم فيقول أحدهم: كان أبي يطعم الطعام

DURR-FULL:v1p557/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r1.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r1.claim: The continuation of Anas's report gives further boasts about fathers: one wielded a sword and another clipped forelocks.
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r1.anchor: ويقول الآخر: كان أبي يضرب بالسيف ويقول الآخر: كان أبي يجز بالنواصي فنزلت

DURR-FULL:v1p557/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r2.claim: Said b. Jubayr and Ikrima say people recalled their fathers' pre-Islamic deeds while standing at Arafah, prompting the verse.
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة قالا: كانوا يذكرون فعل آبائهم في الجاهلية إذا وقفوا بعرفة

DURR-FULL:v1p557/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r3.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r3.claim: Ata says pilgrims at Mina boasted about fathers and gatherings and deeds, and were commanded to remember God instead.
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r3.anchor: عن عطاء قال: كان أهل الجاهلية إذا نزلوا منى تفاخروا بآبائهم ومجالسهم

DURR-FULL:v1p557/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r4.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r4.claim: Ata b. Abi Rabah interprets the comparison to remembering fathers as the first words a child articulates: father and mother.
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r4.anchor: عن عطاء بن أبي رباح في قوله {فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا} قال: هو قول الصبي

DURR-FULL:v1p557/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says stronger remembrance means being more incensed when God is disobeyed than when one's parents are insulted, not remembering one's father all day.
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قيل له: قول الله {كذكركم آباءكم} أن الرجل ليأتي عليه اليوم

DURR-FULL:v1p557/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says Bedouins asked only for worldly rain, abundance, and good offspring at pilgrimage, while believers asked for good in both worlds and protection from the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان قوم من الأعراب يجيئون إلى الموقف فيقولون: اللهم اجعله عام غيث

DURR-FULL:v1p557/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r7.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says pre-Islamic pilgrims at the Sacred Station prayed for camels or sheep, occasioning the worldly-only prayer.
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الزبير قال: كان الناس في الجاهلية إذا وقفوا عند المشعر الحرام دعوا

DURR-FULL:v1p557/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r8.speaker: أنس بن مالك
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r8.claim: Anas says people performing naked circumambulation prayed for rain, victory over enemies, and a safe return to their people.
DURR-FULL:v1p557/r8.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك في قوله {فمن الناس من يقول ربنا آتنا في الدنيا} قال: كانوا يطوفون بالبيت عراة

DURR-FULL:v1p559/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p559/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v1p559/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd contrasts worldly-only petitioners, who made pilgrimage for this life and disbelieve in the afterlife, with those asking for good in both worlds; he connects a third type to 2:204.
DURR-FULL:v1p559/r7.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال: كانوا أصنافا ثلاثة في تلك المواطن يومئذ: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم والمؤمنون

IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r1.claim: Mujahid explains completing the rites as shedding the sacrificial blood.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ، قوله : فاذا قضيتم مناسككم قال : اهراقة الدماء .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r2.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r2.claim: Ata interprets completing the rites as completing the Hajj.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r2.anchor: عن عطاء : فاذا قضيتم مناسككم قال : حجكم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas rejects the idea that the verse simply means to mention one's father daily; it commands anger for God at disobedience greater than anger when one's father is insulted.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r3.anchor: قلت لابن عباس : قول الله : كذكركم ابائكم أو اشد ذكرا قال : ان الرجل لياتي عليه اليوم و ما يذكر اباه . قال : انه ليس بذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، أنس بن مالك، أبو وائل، عطاء بن أبي رباح، سعيد بن جبير، عكرمة، مجاهد، السدي، عطاء الخراساني، الربيع بن أنس، الحسن، قتادة، محمد بن كعب، مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r4.claim: At pilgrimage gatherings, pre-Islamic Arabs boasted of their fathers' feeding, burden-bearing, and payment of blood money; the verse redirected such remembrance to God, or more.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قال : كان أهل الجاهلية يقفون في المواسم ، فيقول الرجل منهم : كان أبي يطعم و يحمل الحمالات و يحمل الديات

IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r5.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r5.claim: Ata interprets the comparison through a child first babbling for its father and mother.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r5.anchor: عن عطاء : فاذكروا الله كذكركم ابائكم قال : هو الصبي اول ما يلهج من الكلام : يا ابه ، ياامه .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r6.speaker: عكرمة، الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r6.claim: Ikrima says the comparison is a father's remembrance of his child, since a parent is entrusted with the child; al-Dahhak is reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p355/r6.anchor: سالت عكرمة عن قول الله : فاذكروا الله كذكركم ابائكم : اهو ذكرى ابي ؟ قال : لا ، ولكن ذكر ابيك اياك

IBNABIHATIM:v2p356/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p356/r1.speaker: ابن الزبير، محمد بن كعب
IBNABIHATIM:v2p356/r1.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says pilgrims used to boast of their fathers after Hajj, so God commanded remembrance of Him as they remembered their fathers; Muhammad ibn Ka'b is reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p356/r1.anchor: عن ابن الزبير : فاذكروا الله كذكركم ابائكم قال : كانوا اذا فرغوا من حجهم ، تفاخروا بابائهم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p356/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p356/r2.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p356/r2.claim: Muqatil says that since God did good to people and their fathers, they must remember God more intensely than their fathers.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p356/r2.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان قوله : فاذكروا الله كذكركم ابائكم أو اشد ذكرا فاني ان فعلت الخير بكم وبابائكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r1.claim: The command follows the departure from Muzdalifa to Mina, explicitly or by implication; Mina is where stoning occurs, and the verse points to stoning Aqaba on the tenth, then sacrifice and completion of Hajj.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r1.anchor: لأن تلك الإفاضة هي الدفع من مزدلفة إلى منى أو لأنها تستلزم ذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r2.claim: Scholars agree that on the Day of Sacrifice the pilgrim stones only Aqaba, from sunrise until noon, then sacrifices, performs the circumambulation of ifada, and completes Hajj; all becomes permitted except sex.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r2.anchor: وقد أجمعوا على أن الحاج لا يرمي يوم النحر إلا جمرة العقبة من بعد طلوع الشمس إلى الزوال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r3.claim: مناسك is the plural of mansak, from worship; here it is best taken as a verbal noun after قضيتم, though it could mean a place and require an omitted noun. The same term occurs in 2:128.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r3.anchor: منسك مشتق من نسك نسكا من باب نصر إذا تعبد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r4.claim: All readers pronounce the two ك sounds separately; al-Susi from Abu Amr merges them by the major assimilation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p244#2/r4.anchor: بفك الكافين وقرأه السوسي عن أبي عمرو بإدغامهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r1.claim: The renewed command encourages remembrance after remembrance and asking forgiveness, countering pre-Islamic idle talk and boasting that led to argument; pilgrims should be immersed in worship in deed, speech, and belief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r1.anchor: أعاد الأمر بالذكر بعد أن أمر به وبالاستغفار تحضيضا عليه وإبطالا لما كانوا عليه في الجاهلية من الاشتغال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r2.claim: The comparison describes the manner of remembrance; the prepositional phrase modifies an omitted verbal noun, “remembrance.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r2.anchor: فالجار والمجرور نعت لمصدر محذوف أي ذكرا كذكركم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r3.claim: The comparison recalls pilgrims filling their time at Mina by boasting about ancestry and past tribal exploits between the mosque site and the mountain beginning at the Aqaba stoning place.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r3.anchor: إشارة إلى ما كانوا عليه من الاشتغال في أيام منى بالتفاخر بالأنساب ومفاخر أيامهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r4.claim: Al-Suddi reports that a man would boast that his father had a great tent, a large bowl, and much wealth, then ask God for the same; he would mention nothing else, and similar statements were reported.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r4.anchor: كان الرجل يقوم فيقول : اللهم إن أبي كان عظيم القبة عظيم الجفنة كثير المال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r5.claim: The comparison calls for frequent, repeated remembrance that fills free time; it does not suggest combining remembrance of God with remembrance of fathers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245/r5.anchor: والمراد تشبيه ذكر الله بذكر آبائهم في الكثرة والتكرير وتعمير أوقات الفراغ به وليس فيه ما يؤذن بالجمع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r1.claim: Here aw moves upward from comparison with fathers to stronger remembrance, urging abundant remembrance of God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r1.anchor: معنى من التدرج إلى أعلى ، فالمقصود أن يذكروا الله كثيرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r2.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي وابن جنى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r2.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi and Ibn Jinni take aw as a transitional shift, requiring neither preceding negation nor repetition of the governing word.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي وابن جنى : إن ( أو ) في مثل هذا للإضراب الانتقالي ونفيا اشتراط تقدم نفي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r3.claim: Comparing remembrance of God with forefathers indirectly reproaches pilgrims for useless ancestral boasting and redirects them to God, more deserving of remembrance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r3.anchor: وشبه أولا بذكر آبائهم تعريضا بأنهم يشتغلون في ذلك المناسك بذكر لا ينفع وأن الأجدر بهم أن يعوضوه بذكر الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r4.claim: One parsing coordinates ashadda with an implied accusative verbal noun after the comparison: remembrance like their remembrance of fathers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r4.anchor: معطوفا على مصدر مقدر منصوب على أنه مفعول مطلق بعد قوله { كذكركم آباءكم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r5.claim: On that parse dhikran is a rare synonym tamyiz, accepted because differing word forms let it emphasize ashadda; Ibn Ashur follows al-Zajjaj and notes Sibawayh's examples.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r5.anchor: صار مآل التمييز إلى أنه تمييز الشيء بمرادفه وذلك ينافي القصد من التمييز الذي هو لإزالة الإبهام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r6.claim: Jarir's emphatic tamyiz after niʿma parallels using synonym tamyiz for emphasis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p245#2/r6.anchor: وقريب منه استعمال تمييز ( نعم ) توكيدا في قوله جرير : تزود مثل زاد أبيك فينا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r1.claim: Ashadda can be a circumstantial accusative from dhikr, originally its adjective in the order dhikran ashadda.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r1.anchor: أن يكون نصب { أشد } على الحال من ( ذكر ) الموالي له وأن أصل أشد نعت له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r2.claim: Fronting the adjective foregrounds intensity, sustains the rhyme vowel at a pause, and separates repeated forms of dhikr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r2.anchor: والداعي إلى تقديم النعت حينئذ هو الاهتمام بوصف كونه أشد ، وليتأتى إشباع حرف الفاصلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r3.speaker: الكوفيون وابن مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r3.claim: The Kufians, followed by Ibn Malik and later grammarians, permit coordinating ashadda with the genitive without repeating the preposition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r3.anchor: فالكوفيون لا يمنعونه ووافقهم بعض المتأخرين مثل ابن مالك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r4.speaker: حمزة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r4.claim: Hamza's genitive reading of al-arham at 4:1 exemplifies coordination to a genitive without repeating the preposition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r4.anchor: وعليه قراءة حمزة { واتقوا الله الذي تساءلون به والأرحام } ( النساء : 1 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows coordination to a preposition-governed genitive here and in 4:77.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r5.anchor: وقد أجاز الزمخشري هنا وفي قوله تعالى : { كخشية الله أو أشد خشية في ( سورة النساء : 77 ) أن يكون العطف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r6.speaker: ابن الحاجب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r6.claim: Ibn al-Hajib reports grammarians who allow this only when genitive is by annexation, not a preposition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r6.anchor: وبعض النحويين جوزه فيما إذا كان الجر بالإضافة لا بالحرف كما قاله ابن الحاجب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r7.claim: With genitive coordination, ashadda's fatha substitutes for kasra because it is a diptote; dhikran remains a tamyiz.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r7.anchor: ففتحة { أشد } نائبة عن الكسرة ، لأن أشد ممنوع من الصرف وعلى هذا الوجه فانتصاب { ذكرا } على التمييز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r8.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r8.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects al-Zamakhshari's two other parses as strained attempts to avoid a synonymous tamyiz.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r8.anchor: ولصاحب ( الكشاف ) تخريجان آخران لإعراب { أو أشد ذكرا } فيهما تعسف دعاه إليهما الفرار من ترادف التمييز والمميز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r9.speaker: ابن جني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r9.claim: Ibn Jinni, following Abu Ali, offers a still more strained parse for the same reason; Ibn al-Munir reports it and al-Zamakhshari uses it at 4:77.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r9.anchor: ولابن جني تبعا لشيخه أبي علي تخريج آخر ، دعاه إليه مثل الذي دعا الزمخشري وكان تخريجه أشد تعسفا ذكره عنه ابن المنير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r10.speaker: ابن عرفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r10.claim: Ibn Arafa calls the syntax exceptionally difficult, praises al-Tayyibi's clarification here and at 4:77, and recounts Ibn Abd al-Salam's approval of the book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p246/r10.anchor: قال الشيخ ابن عرفة في ( تفسيره ) ( وهذه مسألة طويلة عويصة ما رأيت من يفهمها من الشيوخ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r1.claim: The fa in fa-min al-nas signals division: the next clause divides those addressed by the remembrance command into two groups.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r1.anchor: الفاء للتفصيل ؛ لأن ما بعدها تقسيم لفريقين من الناس المخاطبين بقوله : { فاذكروا الله }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r2.claim: The general command implicitly includes supplication, especially at sacred places and responsive times; the implied continuation is to remember God and supplicate Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r2.anchor: فقد علم السامعون أن الذكر يشمل الدعاء ؛ لأنه من ذكر الله وخاصة في مظان الإجابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r3.claim: Only supplicants need division into groups: non-supplicatory remembrance has one praiseworthy form, glorifying and praising God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r3.anchor: وإنما لم يفعل الذكر الأعم من الدعاء ، لأن الذكر الذي ليس بدعاء لا يقع إلا على وجه واحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r4.claim: The two groups encompass Muslims and polytheists, since the verse preceded the restriction barring polytheists from pilgrimage.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r4.anchor: والمقسم إلى الفريقين جميع الناس من المسلمين والمشركين ؛ لأن الآية نزلت قبل تحجير الحج على المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r5.claim: Those with no afterlife share are polytheists, whose disbelief explains their worldly-only prayer; the verse indirectly censures them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p247/r5.anchor: فيتعين أن المراد بمن ليس له في الآخرة من خلاق هم المشركون ؛ لأن المسلمين لا يهملون الدعاء لخير الآخرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r2.claim: Mujahid takes “مناسككم” to mean sacrifices and shedding blood.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya understands “مناسككم” as the acts of worship and places of Hajj rites.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r3.anchor: والمناسك عندي العبادات في معالم الحج ومواضع النسك فيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r4.claim: After completing Hajj, centered on standing at Arafat, pilgrims should praise God and remember His blessings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r4.anchor: والمعنى إذا فرغتم من حجكم الذي هو الوقوف بعرفة فاذكروا الله بمحامده وأثنوا عليه بآلائه عندكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r5.claim: This moment is singled out because everyone completes rites together then, while other rites occur at different times.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r5.anchor: وخص هذا الوقت بالقضاء لما يقضي الناس فيه مناسكهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r6.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r6.claim: Arabs boasted of ancestors' courage and generosity at the Jamrah; the verse makes them remember God more than ancestors.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r6.anchor: وكانت عادة العرب إذا قضت حجها تقف عند الجمرة فتتفاخر بالآباء وتذكر أيام أسلافها من بسالة وكرم وغير ذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r7.claim: They compare remembrance to a child's appeal to parents: seek refuge in and call upon God as one did in childhood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وعطاء: معنى الآية اذكروا الله كذكر الأطفال آباءهم وأمهاتهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r8.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r8.claim: Another group says to exalt and defend God's sanctuary, preventing shirk and attacks on religion as one defends family.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r8.anchor: وقالت طائفة: معنى الآية اذكروا الله وعظموه وذبوا عن حرمه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r9.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r9.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi reads “كذكركم آباؤكم,” construing the source noun with its object.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r9.anchor: وقرأ محمد ابن كعب القرظي «كذكركم آباؤكم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r10.claim: On that reading, “أشد” can be genitive with “ذكركم,” or accusative with an implied command to remember God more intensely.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r10.anchor: وأشد في موضع خفض عطفا على «ذكركم» ويجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r11.speaker: أبو وائل والسدي وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r11.claim: They say pre-Islamic people prayed only for worldly interests because they did not know the afterlife; the verse reports this to forbid it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r11.anchor: قال أبو وائل والسدي وابن زيد: كانت عادتهم في الجاهلية أن يدعوا في مصالح الدنيا فقط

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r13.claim: “من” is extra after negation, making the denial comprehensive.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p276/r13.anchor: ومن زائدة لأنها بعد النفي، فهي مستغرقة لجنس الحظوظ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r1.speaker: الحسن وعطاء ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r1.claim: At the pilgrimage gathering, people of the pre-Islamic era boasted of their fathers’ deeds, exploits, and lineages; al-Hasan, ʿAṭāʾ, and Mujāhid report this occasion for the verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r1.anchor: أهل الجاهلية كانوا إذا اجتمعوا بالموسم ذكروا أفعال آبائهم وأيامهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r2.claim: Another occasion report says Arabs commonly swore ‘by your father’ when speaking; al-Hasan relates that the verse was revealed in response.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r2.anchor: والثاني أن العرب كانوا إذا حدثوا أو تكلموا يقولون وأبيك إنهم لفعلوا كذا وكذا فنزلت هذه الآية وهذا مروي عن الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says that at Minā after the rites, a man might ask God to give him what his wealthy father had, mentioning his father rather than God and seeking worldly goods; this occasion prompted the verse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r3.anchor: والثالث انهم كانوا إذا قضوا مناسكهم قام الرجل بمنى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r4.claim: Manāsik means acts of worship; here it may mean all the rites of pilgrimage.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r4.anchor: والمناسك المتعبدات وفي المراد بها هاهنا قولان أحدهما أنها جميع أفعال الحج قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r5.claim: Mujāhid takes the rites in this verse specifically to mean the slaughter of sacrificial animals.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r5.anchor: والثاني أنها إراقة الدماء قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r6.claim: One interpretation takes mentioning fathers as acknowledging them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r6.anchor: وفي ذكرهم آبائهم اربعة أقوال أحدها أنه إقرارهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r7.claim: Another interpretation takes it as swearing by their fathers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r7.anchor: والثاني أنه حلفهم بهم والثالث أنه ذكر إحسان آبائهم إليهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r8.claim: A third explanation is that people recalled their fathers’ kindness to them while forgetting God’s kindness.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r8.anchor: والثالث أنه ذكر إحسان آبائهم إليهم فانهم كانوا يذكرونهم وينسون إحسان الله إليهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r9.speaker: عطاء والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r9.claim: A fourth explanation, related from ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, is that children first learn to speak by naming their fathers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r9.anchor: اول نطقهم بذكر آبائهم روي هذا المعنى عن عطاء و الضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r10.claim: The particle aw here is interpreted either as ‘rather’ (bal) or as ‘and’ (wāw).

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r11.claim: The commentary notes that the meaning of khalāq has already been discussed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p215/r11.anchor: الثاني بمعنى الواو و الخلاق قد تقدم ذكره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r1.claim: God commands abundant remembrance after the rites of pilgrimage are completed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r1.anchor: يأمر تعالى بذكره والإكثار منه بعد قضاء المناسك وفراغها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r2.speaker: عطاء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r2.claim: ʿAta, in Ibn Jurayj’s report, explains the comparison as a child constantly saying “my father, my mother”; believers should similarly keep God’s remembrance on their tongues after pilgrimage.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r3.speaker: الضحاك والربيع بن أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Rabi ibn Anas give the same explanation of constant remembrance, as does Ibn ʿAbbas in al-ʿAwfi’s report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r3.anchor: وكذا قال الضحاك والربيع بن أنس
