IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says pre-Islamic Arabs at pilgrimage boasted that their fathers fed people, bore burdens, and paid blood money, remembering nothing beyond their ancestors’ deeds; God redirected them to remember Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r4.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r5.speaker: أنس بن مالك، وأبو وائل، وعطاء بن أبي رباح، وسعيد بن جبير، وعكرمة، ومجاهد، والسدي، وعطاء الخراساني، والربيع بن أنس، والحسن، وقتادة، ومحمد بن كعب، ومقاتل بن حيان
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r5.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabari report that numerous early authorities also explained the verse as displacing boastful remembrance of ancestors with remembrance of God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r5.anchor: وروي عن أنس بن مالك، وأبي وائل، وعطاء بن أبي رباح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r6.claim: The point of the comparison is to urge frequent remembrance of God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r6.anchor: والمقصود منه الحث على كثرة الذكر لله عز وجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r7.claim: “Or even greater remembrance” is accusative as a specification (tamyiz), with the implied sense “greater than your remembrance of your fathers.”
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r7.anchor: على التمييز، تقديره كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد منه ذكرا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r8.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r8.claim: Here “or” confirms that the description is at least equal and possibly greater, rather than expressing doubt, as in the cited comparisons.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r8.anchor: فليست هاهنا للشك قطعا، وإنما هي لتحقيق الخبر عنه بأنه كذلك أو أزيد منه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r9.claim: After abundant remembrance, God directs people to supplicate, since that is a setting for answered prayer, and censures those who ask only for worldly life while neglecting the Hereafter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r9.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى أرشد إلى دعائه بعد كثرة ذكره، فإنه مظنة الإجابة، وذم من لا يسأله إلا في أمر دنياه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r10.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r10.claim: “No share in the Hereafter” means no portion or allotment there.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r11.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r11.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r11.claim: The condemnation is intended to deter people from resembling those who ask only for worldly benefit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r11.anchor: وتضمن هذا الذم التنفير عن التشبه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r12.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says some Bedouins at the pilgrimage standing place asked for a rainy, fertile year and good offspring but mentioned nothing about the Hereafter; the verse censures them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p557/r12.anchor: كان قوم من الأعراب يجيئون إلى الموقف، فيقولون

JISHUMI:v1p826/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p826/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p826/r1.claim: One view has pilgrims stop the talbiya after reaching Mina and casting the first pebble at the Jamrat al-ʿAqaba; Malik says a resident stops after standing at Arafat, after touching the Black Stone, or upon seeing the House.
JISHUMI:v1p826/r1.anchor: وقال مالك بن أنس: إذا وقف بعرفة فأما المقيم فيقطع التلبية إذا استلم الحجر، وقال مالك بن أنس: إذا رأى البيت.

JISHUMI:v1p826/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p826/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p826/r2.claim: Khalaq is a share of good received according to entitlement; qadaʾ is settling a matter decisively and thoroughly, the root of the title qadi.
JISHUMI:v1p826/r2.anchor: الخلاق: النصيب من الخير على تقدير الاستحقاق. والقضاء: فصل الأمر على إحكام،

JISHUMI:v1p826/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p826/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p826/r3.claim: Ashadda dhikran may be governed by the comparison ka- and put in the genitive, or by the verb udhkuru and put in the accusative.
JISHUMI:v1p826/r3.anchor: فيه وجهان: أحدهما: الكاف فيكون موضعه جرا، والآخر الفعل في (اذكروا)

JISHUMI:v1p826/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p826/r4.speaker: الحسن وجماعة
JISHUMI:v1p826/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and others interpret the rites as the pilgrimage and the devotional acts commanded to pilgrims; Mujahid instead says they are sacrificial animals.
JISHUMI:v1p826/r4.anchor: قيل: حجكم، وما أمرتم به في التعبدات، عن الحسن وجماعة،

JISHUMI:v1p826/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p826/r5.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v1p826/r5.claim: Mujahid interprets the rites as sacrificial animals.
JISHUMI:v1p826/r5.anchor: وقيل: الذبائح، عن مجاهد (فاذكروا الله) قيل: هذا يجب

JISHUMI:v1p826/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p826/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p826/r6.claim: One view makes remembering God obligatory after the rites are completed; another takes the command to apply while completing them.
JISHUMI:v1p826/r6.anchor: قيل: هذا يجب بعد قضاء المناسك، وقيل: مع قضاء المناسك، وتقديره:

JISHUMI:v1p826/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p826/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p826/r7.claim: Remembrance is glossed as takbir during the days at Mina because it is distinctive to those days, as all supplications, or as affirmation of divine unity and glorification, the latter reported from Abu Muslim.
JISHUMI:v1p826/r7.anchor: قيل: التكبير أيام منى؛ لأنه الذكر المختص في هذه الأيام، وقيل: سائر الأدعية،

JISHUMI:v1p826/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p826/r8.speaker: أنس والحسن وقتادة
JISHUMI:v1p826/r8.claim: Anas, al-Hasan, and Qatada say people used to mention their fathers and boast of them forcefully; they should remember God at least as intensely, or more because of his blessings.
JISHUMI:v1p826/r8.anchor: أو أشد ذكرا لما له عليكم من النعمة، عن أنس والحسن وقتادة.

JISHUMI:v1p826/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p826/r9.speaker: عطاء والربيع والضحاك
JISHUMI:v1p826/r9.claim: ʿAta, al-Rabiʿ, and al-Dahhak compare invoking God for help with a child calling for his father.
JISHUMI:v1p826/r9.anchor: كذكر الصبي لأبيه، إذ قال: يا أبت في قول عطاء والربيع والضحاك.

JISHUMI:v1p826/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p826/r10.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p826/r10.claim: Abu Muslim says not to forget the benefactor in any circumstance, just as one does not forget one’s parents.
JISHUMI:v1p826/r10.anchor: وقيل: لا تنسوا المنعم في الأحوال كما لا تنسوا الآباء، عن أبي مسلم،

JISHUMI:v1p826/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p826/r11.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p826/r11.claim: Abu ʿAli says people were habituated to repeated mention of their fathers, so they were ordered to remember God to that degree.
JISHUMI:v1p826/r11.anchor: وقيل: كانوا يلهجون بذكر الآباء فأمر بذكره على هذا الحد، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v1p826/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p826/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p826/r12.claim: Aw can function like wa, while ashadda dhikran may mean more remembrance or better remembrance.
JISHUMI:v1p826/r12.anchor: يعني وأشد ذكرا، (أو) بمعنى الواو، وقيل: أكثر ذكرا، وقيل: أحسن ذكرا فمن الناس

JISHUMI:v1p826/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p826/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p826/r13.claim: Some people ask only for worldly goods such as camels, sheep, and servants, and have no share in the afterlife.
JISHUMI:v1p826/r13.anchor: أعطنا من أموال الدنيا إبلا وغنما وعبيدا ونحو ذلك وما له في الآخرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r1.claim: Manāsik means acts of worship or ritual observances; here it has two reported interpretations.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r1.anchor: أما المناسك , فهي المتعبدات , وفيها ها هنا تأويلان

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r2.claim: Mujahid takes the rites completed as the sacrificial animals.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r2.anchor: أحدهما : أنها الذبائح , وهذا قول مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r3.speaker: الحسن البصري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r3.claim: Hasan al-Basri takes the rites as all the acts commanded during pilgrimage.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r3.anchor: والثاني : ما أمروا بفعله في الحج , وهذا قول الحسن البصري

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r4.claim: One interpretation of remembering God is saying the takbir on the days of Mina.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r4.anchor: أحدهما : أن هذا الذكر هو التكبير في أيام منى

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r5.claim: Another interpretation is all the prescribed supplications at the various stations of pilgrimage.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r5.anchor: والثاني : أنه جميع ما سن من الأدعية في مواطن الحج كلها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r6.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r6.claim: Mujahid and Qatada say that after pilgrimage in pre-Islamic times people gathered at Mina to boast of their ancestors' achievements, so God commanded them to remember Him instead.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r6.anchor: وهذا قول مجاهد , وقتادة . والثاني : أن معناه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r7.speaker: عطاء، الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r7.claim: Ata and Dahhak compare the remembrance to small children calling repeatedly for their parents.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r7.anchor: أن معناه , فاذكروا الله كذكركم الأبناء الصغار للآباء , إذا قالوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r8.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says people used to ask for what their fathers had possessed, mentioning the fathers rather than God, so they were told to remember God as intensely.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p262/r8.anchor: أبيه , فأمروا بذكر الله , كذكرهم آباءهم

MUJAHID:v1p103#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p103#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p103#3/r1.claim: The worldly request is for victory and provision, with no request for anything in the Hereafter.
MUJAHID:v1p103#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ فمن الناس من يقول ربنا آتنا في الدنيا ﴾ يعني نصرا ورزقا ولا يسأل لآخرته شيئا

MUQATIL:2:199-201/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:199-201/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:199-201/r3.claim: After the pilgrimage rites, people gathered between Mina's mosque and the mountain to recount their fathers' merits and pre-Islamic deeds and pray for them; God directs them to remember Him instead, since He did good to their ancestors.
MUQATIL:2:199-201/r3.anchor: وذلك أنهم كانوا إذا فرغوا من المناسك وقفوا بين مسجد منى وبين الجبل يذكر كل واحد منهم أباه ومحاسنه،

MUQATIL:2:199-201/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:199-201/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:199-201/r4.claim: Or stronger means more remembrance of God than their remembrance of their fathers.
MUQATIL:2:199-201/r4.anchor: ثم قال سبحانه: { أو أشد } ، يعنى أكثر { ذكرا } لله منكم لآبائكم، وكانوا إذا قضوا

MUQATIL:2:199-201/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:199-201/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:199-201/r5.claim: Arab polytheists prayed after pilgrimage for wealth, children, livestock, long life, rain, pasture, safe travel, and victory, but asked nothing for the afterlife; they therefore have no afterlife share. Khalaq means share, as in 9:69.
MUQATIL:2:199-201/r5.anchor: وكانوا إذا قضوا مناسكهم قالوا: اللهم أكثر أموالنا، وأبناءنا، ومواشينا، وأطل بقاءنا،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r1.claim: After finishing the acts prescribed in pilgrimage and departing, people should remember God.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r1.anchor: فإذا فرغتم من عباداتكم التى أمرتم بها فى الحج ونفرتم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r2.claim: Remember God abundantly, as people recounted and boasted of their ancestors’ merits and achievements.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r2.anchor: فأكثروا من ذكر الله وبالغوا فيه كما تفعلون فى ذكر آبائكم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r3.claim: After pilgrimage, Arabs gathered between the mosque at Mina and the mountain to recount ancestors’ virtues and famous days.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r3.anchor: وكانوا إذا قضوا مناسكهم وقفوا بين المسجد بمنى وبين الجبل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r4.claim: أشد ذكرا means more abundant remembrance; grammatically أشد is genitive by coordination and ذكرا is specification.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r4.anchor: أى أكثر وهو فى موضع جر عطف على ما أضيف إليه الذكر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r5.claim: The comparison is to Quraysh’s remembrance of ancestors or to a people who surpassed them in it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r5.anchor: كذكر قريش آباءهم أو قوم أشد منهم ذكرا وذكرا تمييز

NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r6.claim: Among pilgrims are people who ask God only for worldly advantages.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r6.anchor: فمن الذين يشهدون الحج من يسأل الله حظوظ الدنيا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r7.claim: They ask for worldly giving alone, especially status and wealth.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r7.anchor: اجعل إتياننا أى إعطاءنا فى الدنيا خاصة يعنى الجاه والغنى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r8.claim: They have no afterlife share because, as disbelievers, their concern is confined to worldly life; believers should seek both worlds, as in 2:201.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p98#2/r8.anchor: نصيب لأن همه مقصور على الدنيا لكفره بالآخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r1.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r1.claim: Mujahid says the rites are sacrificial animals and the shedding of blood.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: المناسك الذبائح وهراقة الدماء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes the rites as the ceremonies of Hajj, supported by the Prophet’s instruction to learn the rites from him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r2.anchor: وقيل: هي شعائر الحج لقوله عليه السلام:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r3.claim: After performing a Hajj rite, people should remember God and praise Him for His blessings.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r3.anchor: المعنى: فإذا فعلتم منسكا من مناسك الحج فاذكروا الله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r4.claim: Abu Amr assimilates the first kāf into the second in manāsikakum because the consonants are identical.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r4.anchor: وأبو عمرو يدغم الكاف في الكاف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r5.claim: Here qaḍaytum means that the rites were performed and completed, as in the usage for performing Friday prayer.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r6.claim: The verb qaḍāʾ can also describe worship performed outside its prescribed time.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r6.anchor: وقد يعبر بالقضاء عما فعل من العبادات خارج وقتها المحدود لها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r7.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r7.claim: The majority say Arabs used to boast at the Jamra after Hajj about ancestral valor and generosity and ask for worldly blessings like their fathers’; the verse requires more remembrance of God.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r7.anchor: كانت عادة العرب إذا قضت حجها تقف عند الجمرة، فتفاخر بالآباء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء والضحاك والربيع
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ata, al-Dahhak, and al-Rabiʿ interpret the phrase as children’s remembrance of parents: seek God’s aid as children once sought their parents.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وعطاء والضحاك والربيع: معنى الآية واذكروا الله كذكر الأطفال آبائهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r9.speaker: طائفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r9.claim: Another group says to exalt God, defend His sanctuary, and repel those who would introduce polytheism, as people defend and praise their ancestors.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r9.anchor: وقالت طائفة: معنى الآية اذكروا الله وعظموه وذبوا عن حرمه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r10.speaker: أبو الجوزاء وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r10.claim: When Abu al-Jawza asked why the verse matters if people no longer mention their fathers, Ibn Abbas replied that anger at God’s disobedience should exceed anger at an insult to one’s parents.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r10.anchor: وقال أبو الجوزاء لابن عباس: إن الرجل اليوم لا يذكر أباه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r11.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r11.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses the kāf phrase as an accusative verbal noun: “remembrance like your remembrance.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r11.anchor: والكاف من قوله { كذكركم } في موضع نصب أي ذكرا كذكركم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r12.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r12.claim: Al-Zajjaj says aw ashadd may be genitive, coordinated with dhikrikum and meaning “or like stronger remembrance”; because it is an afʿal adjective, it is not declined.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r12.anchor: قال الزجاج: «أو أشد» في موضع خفض عطفا على ذكركم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r13.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r13.claim: Alternatively, aw ashadd is accusative, meaning “remember Him more strongly”; dhikran is accusative as specification.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r13.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب بمعنى أو اذكروه أشد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r14.claim: Min is nominative as the subject, or may be adjectival; “says, Our Lord…” is its relative clause.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r14.anchor: «من» في موضع رفع بالابتداء، وإن شئت بالصفة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r15.claim: The people described as making only this worldly supplication are polytheists.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r16.speaker: أبو وائل والسدي وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r16.claim: Abu Waʾil, al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd say pre-Islamic Arabs prayed only for worldly goods such as livestock and victory, since they did not know or believe in the afterlife.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r16.anchor: قال أبو وائل والسدي وابن زيد: كانت العرب في الجاهلية تدعوا في مصالح الدنيا فقط

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r17.claim: Qurtubi says the warning may also apply to a believer who restricts supplication to worldly matters; “no share” means no share like the one who asks for the afterlife.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r17.anchor: ويجوز أن يتناول هذا الوعيد المؤمن أيضا إذا قصر دعواته في الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r18.claim: Khalaq means a share, and min is extra in the construction; Qurtubi notes that this was discussed earlier.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:200/r18.anchor: والخلاق النصيب. و «من» زائدة وقد تقدم

QASHANI:2:200/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:200/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:200/r1.claim: The phrase means when you have finished the pilgrimage rites.

QASHANI:2:200/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:200/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:200/r2.claim: Do not remain occupied with lineage and worldly boasts that cloud time and harden hearts; sustain varied remembrance and study with companions, preserving purity and guiding others.
QASHANI:2:200/r2.anchor: فلا تكونوا كأهل العادة مشغولين بذكر الأنساب والمفاخرات

QASHANI:2:200/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:200/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:200/r3.claim: Some seek only worldly goods, remember the world, and worship for its sake; aiming low prevents receiving the higher because aspiration remains low and darkness conflicts with light.
QASHANI:2:200/r3.anchor: أي: لا يطلب إلا متاع الدنيا ولا يشتغل إلا بذكرها

RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says that after the pilgrimage and Tashriq days, Arabs stood between Mina’s mosque and the mountain praising their ancestors’ generosity, courage, and kinship, reciting verse and prose for fame; Islam redirected remembrance to God.
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r1.anchor: روى ابن عباس أن العرب كانوا عند الفراغ من حجتهم بعد أيام التشريق يقفون بين مسجد منى وبين الجبل ، ويذكر كل واحد منهم فضائل آبائه في السماحة والحماسة

RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r2.claim: Al-Qaffal transmits Ibn Umar’s account of the Prophet at the conquest: after praising God, he condemned tribal pride and ranked people by piety or wickedness, reciting 49:13.
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r2.anchor: وروى القفال في ( تفسيره ) عن ابن عمر قال : طاف رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على راحلته القصوى يوم الفتح يستلم الركن بمحجنه ثم حمد الله وأثنى عليه

RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r3.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse was revealed about men at Mina boasting that their fathers had abundant food, rank, and wealth, and asking God to grant them the same.
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r3.anchor: وعن السدي أن العرب بمنى بعد فراغهم من الحج كان أحدهم يقول : اللهم إن أبي كان عظيم الجفنة ، عظيم القدر ، كثير المال ، فأعطني مثل ما أعطيته ، فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآية .

RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r4.claim: When qada is attached to one’s own action it means completion, as in completing the heavens and finishing prayer; the Prophet’s instruction to make up what was missed uses the same sense.
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r4.anchor: نظير الأول قوله تعالى : { فقضاهن سبع * سماوات * فى يومين

RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r5.claim: When qada is attached to another’s action it means imposing or commanding it, as in “your Lord decreed.”
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r5.anchor: ونظير الثاني قوله تعالى : { وقضى ربك } ( الإسراء : 23 ) وإذا استعمل

RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r6.claim: When qada is used for communication it means informing, as in God informing the Children of Israel in scripture.
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r6.anchor: وإذا استعمل في الإعلام ، فالمراد أيضا ذلك كقوله : { وقضينا إلى بنى إسراءيل فى الكتاب } ( الإسراء : 4 )

RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r7.claim: Here “when you have completed your rites” means finishing all Hajj rites, especially since many were already described; the alternative reading as remembrance during Hajj is weak because qada signals completion.
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r7.anchor: إذا ثبت هذا فنقول : قوله تعالى : { فإذا قضيتم مناسككم } لا يحتمل إلا الفراغ من جميعه خصوصا وذكر كثير منه قد تقدم من قبل

RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r8.claim: An alternative takes the command as remembrance during the rites, including prescribed prayers at Arafat, the Sacred Monument, and during circumambulation and saʿy; al-Razi rejects it as inconsistent with completion language.
RAZI-FULL:v5p156#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم : يحتمل أن يكون المراد : اذكروا الله عند المناسك ويكون المراد من هذا الذكر ما أمروا به من الدعاء بعرفات والمشعر الحرام والطواف والسعي

RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r1.claim: Manasik may be the plural of mansek as a verbal noun like nusk, meaning the Hajj acts of worship; if it means places of worship, “acts of your rites” is understood with an omitted noun.
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r1.anchor: ( المناسك ) جمع منسك الذي هو المصدر بمنزلة النسك ، أي إذا قضيتم عباداتكم التي أمرتم بها في الحج

RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r2.claim: Some commentators take the rites here as all the acts of worship God commanded during Hajj.
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r2.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين : المراد من المناسك ههنا ما أمر الله تعالى به الناس في الحج من العبادات

RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r3.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r3.claim: Mujahid says completing the rites means slaughtering the sacrificial animals.
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r3.anchor: وعن مجاهد أن قضاء المناسك هو إراقة الدماء

RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r4.claim: The coordinating fa indicates that completing the rites occasions the commanded remembrance, prompting disagreement about which remembrance is meant.
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r4.anchor: الفاء في قوله : { فاذكروا الله } يدلي على أن الفراغ من المناسك يوجب هذا الذكر

RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r5.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r5.claim: One interpretation makes the remembrance the invocation said over the sacrificial animal.
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r5.anchor: فمنهم من حمله على الذكر على الذبيحة

RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r6.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r6.claim: Another interpretation is the takbir after prayers on the Day of Sacrifice and the Tashriq days, since no other specific remembrance follows Hajj; scholars differ on its time.
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r6.anchor: ومنهم من حمله على الذكر الذي هو التكبيرات بعد الصلاة في يوم النحر وأيام التشويق / على حسب اختلافهم

RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r7.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r7.claim: Another interpretation redirects people from their customary post-Hajj boasting about ancestors to remembrance of God; without the verse, they would have continued that blameworthy practice.
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r7.anchor: ومنهم من قال : بل المراد تحويل القوم عما اعتادوه بعد الحج من ذكر التفاخر بأحوال الآباء لأنه تعالى لو لم ينه عن ذلك بإنزال هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r8.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r8.claim: Another view turns pilgrims after Hajj to supplication, humility, and abundant seeking of forgiveness in response to leaving home, spending wealth, and enduring hardship; this resembles supplication after prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r8.anchor: ومنهم من قال : بل المراد منه أن الفراغ من الحج يوجب الإقبال على الدعاء والاستغفار ، وذلك لأن من تحمل مفارقة الأهل والوطن

RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r9.claim: An inward reading sees Hajj rites as subduing the lower self and erasing its false impressions; afterward the heart is illumined by God’s remembrance, first negating all but the Real, then affirming Him.
RAZI-FULL:v5p157/r9.anchor: وفيه وجه خامس وهو أن المقصود من الاشتغال بهده العبادة : قهر النفس ومحو آثار النفس والطبيعة

RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r1.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r1.claim: The majority say to devote as much effort to praising God and recounting His favors as Arabs devoted to ancestors; ancestor boasts are falsehood deserving punishment or truthful pride and arrogance, so God’s remembrance is superior, or at least equal.
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r1.anchor: وهو قول جمهور المفسرين : أنا ذكرنا أن القوم كانوا بعد الفراغ من الحج يبالغون في الثناء على آبائهم في ذكر مناقبهم وفضائلهم

RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r2.speaker: الضحاك والربيع
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Rabiʿ compare remembrance of God to a child’s constant calling for father and mother; “fathers” can stand for both parents, as in 16:81.
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r2.anchor: قال الضحاك والربيع : اذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم وأمهاتكم

RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r3.claim: Abu Muslim takes ancestors as an example of constant remembrance: just as a person does not forget his father, he should not neglect remembrance of God.
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r3.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : جرى ذكر الآباء مثلا لدوام الذكر

RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says Arabs commonly swore by their fathers in pre-Islamic times, so the command redirects their reverence toward God.
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r4.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري في هذه الآية : إن العرب كان أكثر أقسامها في الجاهلية بالآباء

RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r5.speaker: بعض المذكورين
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r5.claim: Another interpretation says to affirm God’s oneness as people affirm their ancestors’ oneness; indeed, monotheistic insistence is even more fitting for God.
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r5.anchor: قال بعض المذكورين : المعنى اذكروا الله بالوحدانية كذكركم آبائكم بالوحدانية

RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r6.claim: A further analogy is the child who turns to his father for every need and remembers him reverently; believers should relate to God’s remembrance in the same way.
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r6.anchor: وسادسها : أن الطفل كما يرجع إلى أبيه في طلب جميع المهمات ويكون ذاكرا له بالتعظيم ، فكونوا أنتم في ذكر الله كذلك

RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r7.claim: Another view says people invoked ancestors as intermediaries for answered prayers, but their deeds were invalidated by shirk; instead recount God’s favors and praise Him for future blessings.
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r7.anchor: يحتمل أنهم كانوا يذكرون آباءهم ليتوسلوا بذكره إلى إجابة الدعاء عند الله فعرفهم الله تعالى أن آباءهم ليسوا في هذه الدرجة إذ أفعالهم الحسنة صارت غير معتبرة بسبب شركهم

RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r8.claim: The Prophet forbids swearing by one’s ancestors, instructing anyone who swears to swear by God or remain silent; God alone deserves exaltation.
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r8.anchor: وقد نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أن يحلفوا بآبائهم فقال : ( من كان حالفا فليحلف بالله أو ليصمت )

RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the verse as becoming more angry on God’s behalf when He is disobeyed than when one’s parent is insulted.
RAZI-FULL:v5p158/r9.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال في تفسير هذه الآية : هو أن تغضب لله إذا عصى أشد من غضبك لوالدك إذا ذكر بسوء

RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r1.claim: Al-Razi deems the first interpretation decisive; all the readings converge on constant remembrance, honoring God, seeking needs from Him, and turning away from all else.
RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r1.anchor: وإن كانت محتملة إلا أن الوجه الأول هو المتعين وجميع الوجوه مشتركة في شيء واحد ، وهو أنه يجب على العبد أن يكون دائم الذكر لربه دائم التعظيم له

RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r2.claim: “Ashadd” may be genitive, governed by the comparison kāf, or accusative, governed by “remember”: remember God like the ancestors, and remember Him more intensely than them.
RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r2.anchor: عامل الإعراب في { أشد } قيل : الكاف ، فيكون موضعه جرا وقيل : { اذكروا } فيكون موضعه نصبا ، والتقدير

RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r3.claim: Here “or” means “rather, more”: ancestors’ merits are limited, while God’s perfection attributes are endless, so remembering Him should be more intense.
RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r3.anchor: قوله : { أو أشد ذكرا } معناه : بل أشد ذكرا ، وذلك لأن مفاخر آبائهم كانت قليلة ، أما صفات الكمال لله عز وجل

RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r4.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r4.claim: Al-Qaffal explains this comparative phrasing as ordinary Arabic usage for moving from an initial term to something sooner, not expressing uncertainty, as in “do this by a month or sooner.”
RAZI-FULL:v5p158#2/r4.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله : ومجاز اللغة

QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r1.claim: Completing pilgrimage rites signifies fulfilling the body's duty of servanthood; remembering God like one's fathers signifies the heart's duty of love, sustained throughout life.
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r1.anchor: قضيتم مناسككم } إشارة إلى القيام بحق العبودية .

QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r2.claim: Since people take pride in their ancestors, the faithful should take pride and joy in God; His claim and favors exceed those of their forebears.
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r2.anchor: ويقال كما أن الأغيار يفتخرون بآبائهم ، ويستبشرون بأسلافهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r3.claim: Parents have a claim through upbringing, but God's claim is greater and His favors more complete; His majesty exceeds ancestors' good qualities.
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r3.anchor: ويقال إن كان لآبائكم عليكم حق التربية فحقنا عليكم أوجب ، وأفضالنا عليكم أتم

QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r4.claim: As one does not tire of remembering one's father, one should persist in remembering God without weariness, boredom, or forgetfulness.
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r4.anchor: ويقال إنك لا تمل ذكر أبيك ولا تنساه على غالب أحوالك ، فاستدم ذكرنا

QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r5.claim: Just as one resists attacks on one's lineage, one should defend God against the claims of people of error and innovation.
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r5.anchor: إن طعن في نسبك طاعن لم ترض فكذلك ما تسمع من أقاويل أهل الضلال والبدع

QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r6.claim: Remember God with reverent awe and gentle intimacy; fathers are remembered respectfully, mothers compassionately, while God shows mercy and is not an object of mercy.
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r6.anchor: الأب يذكر بالحرمة والحشمة فكذلك اذكرنا بالهيبة مع ذكر لطيف القربة

QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r7.claim: The verse names fathers rather than mothers because fathers are remembered with reverence, whereas mothers are remembered with compassion.
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r7.anchor: وقال { كذكركم آباءكم } ولم يقل أمهاتكم لأن الأب يذكر احتراما

QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r8.claim: God deserves more remembrance than fathers, and a knower may feel estranged from a father but cannot conceive of God failing what is due.
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r8.anchor: لأن الحق أحق ، ولأنك قد تستوحش كثيرا عن أبيك

QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r9.claim: A father is remembered according to what he merits, and the Lord according to what He merits.
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r9.anchor: الأب علىما يستحقه والرب على ما يستحقه

QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r10.claim: A creature would count such a request as gratitude, yet God graciously permits people to bring complaints to Him; some hearts still settle for their worldly share.
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r10.anchor: فقال : من الناس من لا يجنح قلبه إلينا ، ويرضى بدوننا عنا

QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r11.claim: The worldly good that gathers every good is preservation of faith through death; the afterlife good that gathers all good is forgiveness.
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r11.anchor: والحسنة التي بها تحصل جميع الحسنات في الدنيا - حفظ الإيمان عليهم في المآل

QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r12.claim: Another reading calls the world's good renunciation of it and the next world's good protection from settling in it; refuge from the Fire includes the flames of separation and burning longing.
QUSHAYRI:v1p97/r12.anchor: ويقال الحسنة في الدنيا العزوف عنها ، والحسنة في الآخرة الصون عن مساكنتها

RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī says jinn and devils are not ordinary dense bodies moving about like humans and animals; he outlines two other accounts of their nature.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r1.anchor: أطبق الكل على أنه ليس الجن والشياطين عبارة عن أشخاص جسمانية كثيفة تجيء وتذهب مثل الناس والبهائم

RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r2.speaker: القول الأول
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r2.claim: One account makes jinn and devils airy bodies that can assume different forms, reason, understand, and perform difficult tasks.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r2.anchor: الأول أنها أجسام هوائية قادرة على التشكل بأشكال مختلفة ولها عقول وأفهام

RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r3.speaker: كثير من الناس
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r3.claim: A second account, held by many, makes them immaterial entities, neither occupying space nor inhering in bodies.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r3.anchor: أن كثيرا من الناس أثبتوا أنها موجودات غير متحيزة ولا حالة في المتحيز

RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r4.claim: On the immaterial account, spirits range from exalted angels to spirits managing bodies, including ranks linked to the Throne, Kursī, celestial spheres, seas, mountains, plants, and animals.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r4.anchor: ثم هذه الموجودات قد تكون عالية مقدسة عن تدبير الأجسام بالكلية وهي الملائكة المقربون

RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r5.claim: On either account, benevolent, luminous spirits are called righteous jinn, while low, dark, evil spirits are called devils.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r5.anchor: قد تكون مشرقة إلهية خيرة سعيدة وهي المسماة بالصالحين من الجن

RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r6.speaker: المنكرون لوجود الجن والشياطين
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r6.claim: The deniers argue that jinn must be either dense bodies, which healthy senses would see, or subtle bodies, which violent winds would tear and which could not perform the difficult acts attributed to them.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r6.anchor: احتج المنكرون لوجود الجن والشياطين بوجوه : الحجة الأولى

RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r7.speaker: المنكرون لوجود الجن والشياطين
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r7.claim: They also argue that long contact with humans should create visible friendship or hostility and resulting benefits or harms, yet none is observed; even repentant conjurers deny seeing effects.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69#3/r7.anchor: إذا كانوا حاضرين في هذا العالم مخالطين للبشر فالظاهر الغالب أن يصل لهم بسبب طول المخالطة

STUDYQURAN:2:200/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:200/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:200/r1.claim: Rites may mean the animal sacrifice at Eid al-Adha, which marks the end of the Hajj, or all Hajj rituals whose essential purpose is remembrance of God.
STUDYQURAN:2:200/r1.anchor: or the Feast of Sacrifice, marking the end of the ḥajj

STUDYQURAN:2:200/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:200/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:200/r2.claim: One interpretation recalls Arabs’ post-Hajj custom of celebrating ancestors’ past glories through competitive boasting.
STUDYQURAN:2:200/r2.anchor: custom of the Arabs, at the conclusion of the ḥajj, of engaging in the magnification and celebration

STUDYQURAN:2:200/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:200/r3.speaker: Others
STUDYQURAN:2:200/r3.claim: Others say one should remember and call upon God as a helpless, dependent child calls upon mother and father, trusting completely.
STUDYQURAN:2:200/r3.anchor: Others interpret remember God as you remember your fathers to mean that one should call upon and remember God the way a small child calls upon mother and father

TAB-FULL:v3p535/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p535/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p535/r1.claim: When people have finished Hajj and slaughtered their sacrificial animals, they should remember Allah.
TAB-FULL:v3p535/r1.anchor: إذا ذبح نسكه، والمنسك: اسم مثل المشرق والمغرب.

TAB-FULL:v3p535/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p535/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p535/r2.claim: In this context manāsik means sacrificial slaughter: the verb nasaka may describe slaughtering a sacrifice, and mansak is a noun patterned like mashriq or maghrib; religious nasak can also mean devotion and worship.
TAB-FULL:v3p535/r2.anchor: الرجل ينسك نسكا ونسكا ونسيكة ومنسكا إذا ذبح نسكه، والمنسك: اسم مثل المشرق والمغرب.

TAB-FULL:v3p535/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p535/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p535/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses completing the rites as shedding the sacrificial blood.
TAB-FULL:v3p535/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {فإذا قضيتم مناسككم} [البقرة: 200] قال: إهراقه الدماء "

TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r1.speaker: أنس
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r1.claim: Anas reports that pre-Islamic Arabs gathered after pilgrimage to boast about their fathers; Muslims were ordered to praise, thank, magnify, and remember their Lord at least as much.
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r1.anchor: عن أنس، في هذه الآية، قال: " كانوا يذكرون آباءهم في الحج، فيقول بعضهم: كان أبي يطعم الطعام

TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r2.speaker: أنس
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r2.claim: Anas says people recalled fathers’ reputations at Hajj: one fed others, another fought with a sword, and another cut the forelocks of a tribe’s men.
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r2.anchor: عن أنس، في هذه الآية، قال: " كانوا يذكرون آباءهم في الحج، فيقول بعضهم: كان أبي يطعم الطعام، ويقول بعضهم: كان أبي

TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r3.claim: Mujahid says they boasted that their fathers slaughtered camels and did other deeds, prompting the verse’s command to remember Allah.
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: " كانوا يقولون: كان آباؤنا ينحرون الجزر، ويفعلون كذا، فنزلت هذه الآية:

TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r4.speaker: أبو وائل
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r4.claim: Abu Wail explains the verse as replacing the pre-Islamic habit of recalling fathers’ deeds.
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r4.anchor: عن عاصم، عن أبي وائل: " {فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا} [البقرة: 200] قال: كان أهل الجاهلية

TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r5.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r5.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash says that after Hajj people stood by the House recalling their fathers, their days, and their deeds.
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r5.anchor: سمعت أبا بكر بن عياش، قال: " كان أهل الجاهلية

TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r6.claim: Mujahid reports that pilgrims stopped at the jamrah and recalled their pre-Islamic days and fathers’ deeds; the verse was revealed in response.
TAB-FULL:v3p535#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {اذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم} قال: كانوا إذا قضوا مناسكهم وقفوا عند الجمرة فذكروا آباءهم،

TAB-FULL:v3p538/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p538/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p538/r1.claim: Mujahid says the Arabs boasted of their fathers’ deeds after finishing the rites on the day of sacrifice, and were told to remember Allah instead.
TAB-FULL:v3p538/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {فإذا قضيتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم} [البقرة: 200] قال: تفاخرت العرب بينها بفعل آبائها يوم النحر حين فرغوا، فأمروا بذكر الله مكان ذلك "

TAB-FULL:v3p538/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p538/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v3p538/r2.claim: Qatada says pilgrims at Mina sat in circles recalling and boasting of their fathers’ deeds, while speakers addressed the group; Allah ordered remembrance of Him equally or more.
TAB-FULL:v3p538/r2.anchor: عن قتادة: {فإذا قضيتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم} [البقرة: 200] قال قتادة:

TAB-FULL:v3p538/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p538/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعكرمة
TAB-FULL:v3p538/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr and ʿIkrima report that people recalled their fathers’ deeds in pre-Islamic times while standing at Arafat, whereupon the verse was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v3p538/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، وعكرمة، قالا: «كانوا يذكرون فعل آبائهم في الجاهلية إذا وقفوا بعرفة، فنزلت هذه الآية»

TAB-FULL:v3p538/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p538/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v3p538/r4.claim: A second view takes the comparison to mean remembering Allah as children remember their parents, or more intensely.
TAB-FULL:v3p538/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل معنى ذلك: فاذكروا الله كذكر الأبناء، والصبيان الآباء

TAB-FULL:v3p538/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p538/r5.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v3p538/r5.claim: Ataa illustrates the second view with a child calling out, ‘O father!’
TAB-FULL:v3p538/r5.anchor: عن عثمان بن أبي رواد، عن عطاء، أنه قال في هذه الآية: " {كذكركم آباءكم} [البقرة: 200] قال: هو قول الصبي: يا أباه "

TAB-FULL:v3p539/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets the comparison as children remembering their parents.
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك: " {فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم} [البقرة: 200] يعني بالذكر، ذكر الأبناء الآباء "

TAB-FULL:v3p539/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r2.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r2.claim: Ataa glosses it as a child saying ‘father, mother.’
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قال لي عطاء: " {كذكركم آباءكم} [البقرة: 200] أبه أمه "

TAB-FULL:v3p539/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r3.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r3.claim: Another report from Ataa compares the remembrance to a child constantly babbling about father and mother.
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r3.anchor: عن عطاء، قال: «كالصبي، يلهج بأبيه وأمه»

TAB-FULL:v3p539/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r4.claim: Al-Rabiʿ paraphrases the comparison as children remembering parents, or remembering them even more.
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r4.anchor: عن الربيع، قوله: " {فإذا قضيتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا} [البقرة: 200] يقول: كذكر الأبناء الآباء، أو أشد ذكرا "

TAB-FULL:v3p539/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says to remember Allah as children remember their parents.
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {فإذا قضيتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا} [البقرة: 200] يقول: كما يذكر الأبناء الآباء "

TAB-FULL:v3p539/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r6.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r6.claim: A third view says people used to invoke God after the rites without mentioning Him, asking instead for things associated with their fathers, so they were ordered to remember God with comparable intensity.
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r6.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل قيل لهم: {اذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم} لأنهم كانوا إذا قضوا مناسكهم فدعوا ربهم لم يذكروا غير آبائهم

TAB-FULL:v3p539/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r7.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r7.claim: Al-Suddi describes a pilgrim at Mina asking for the wealth and status his father had, without actually mentioning Allah.
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r7.anchor: عن السدي: " {فإذا قضيتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله

TAB-FULL:v3p539/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r8.claim: Tabari’s preferred reading commands remembrance through obedience, submission, and worship after pilgrimage; this may be the takbir required after completing the rites in 2:203.
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r8.anchor: والصواب من القول عندي في تأويل ذلك أن يقال: إن الله جل ثناؤه أمر عباده المؤمنين بذكره بالطاعة له في الخضوع لأمره والعبادة له بعد قضاء مناسكهم.

TAB-FULL:v3p539/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r9.claim: Tabari reasons that takbir is the special remembrance newly prescribed after the rites; believers should maintain it abundantly and humbly, like children appeal to parents, since all their blessings come from Allah.
TAB-FULL:v3p539/r9.anchor: من أجل أنه لا ذكر لله أمر العباد به بعد قضاء مناسكهم لم يكن عليهم من فرضه قبل قضائهم مناسكهم، سوى التكبير الذي خص الله به أيام منى.

TAB-FULL:v3p542/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r1.claim: After the rites, believers should earnestly seek God’s pleasure and ask Him for good in both this world and the hereafter.
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r1.anchor: وقولوا ربنا آتنا في الدنيا حسنة، وفي الآخرة حسنة، وقنا عذاب النار

TAB-FULL:v3p542/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r2.claim: The verse contrasts those who traded the hereafter for worldly life: their deeds seek worldly adornment and enjoyment, leaving them no share in divine reward or Paradise.
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r2.anchor: ولا تكونوا كمن اشترى الحياة الدنيا بالآخرة، فكانت أعمالهم للدنيا وزينتها، فلا يسألون ربهم إلا متاعها، ولا حظ لهم في ثواب الله

TAB-FULL:v3p542/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r3.speaker: أبو وائل
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r3.claim: Abu Wa'il explains the worldly prayer as asking God for sheep and camels, with no share in the hereafter.
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r3.anchor: عن أبي وائل: " {فمن الناس من يقول ربنا آتنا في الدنيا} [البقرة: 200] هب لنا غنما، هب لنا إبلا

TAB-FULL:v3p542/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r4.claim: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash says people in pre-Islamic times, after completing the rites, asked God for camels and sheep; the verse was revealed about this practice.
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r4.anchor: أبا بكر بن عياش، في قوله: " {فمن الناس من يقول ربنا آتنا في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v3p542/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r5.speaker: أنس
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r5.claim: Anas reports that people circumambulated the House naked and prayed for rain, victory over enemies, and a safe return among the righteous.
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r5.anchor: أنس: " {فمن الناس من يقول ربنا آتنا في الدنيا وما له في الآخرة من خلاق} [البقرة: 200] قال: كانوا يطوفون بالبيت عراة

TAB-FULL:v3p542/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r6.claim: Mujahid glosses the worldly request as victory and provision; these people ask nothing for their hereafter.
TAB-FULL:v3p542/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله تبارك وتعالى: " {فمن الناس من يقول ربنا آتنا في الدنيا} [البقرة: 200] نصرا ورزقا، ولا يسألون

TAB-FULL:v3p544/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p544/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v3p544/r1.claim: Qatada describes this as a servant who intended the world, working and toiling for it.
TAB-FULL:v3p544/r1.anchor: فهذا عبد نوى الدنيا لها عمل ولها نصب

TAB-FULL:v3p544/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p544/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p544/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says Arabs at Mina after completing the rites would remember their fathers rather than God and ask only for worldly provision.
TAB-FULL:v3p544/r2.anchor: عن السدي، في قوله: " {فمن الناس من يقول ربنا آتنا في الدنيا وما له في الآخرة من خلاق} [البقرة: 200] قال: كانت العرب

TAB-FULL:v3p544/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p544/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v3p544/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd classifies pilgrims as the Messenger, unbelievers, and hypocrites: some sought only worldly gains without belief in the hereafter, while others asked for good in both realms and a third group is described at 2:204.
TAB-FULL:v3p544/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله. {فإذا قضيتم مناسككم فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا}

TAB-FULL:v3p544/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p544/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p544/r4.claim: Tabari says he has already established that khalaq here means a share, so he does not repeat that discussion.
TAB-FULL:v3p544/r4.anchor: والصحيح لدينا من معناه بالشواهد من الأدلة وأنه النصيب

TABATABAI:2:198-200/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r3.claim: After pilgrimage rites, worshippers are urged to remember God as they remember their fathers, or more intensely, because God’s gift of guidance gives them a greater claim than their parents.

TABATABAI:2:198-200/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r4.claim: In pre-Islamic practice, Arabs stayed for a time at Minā after pilgrimage and boasted of their forefathers in verse and prose; God replaced this with remembrance of Him.
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r4.anchor: وقد قيل إن العرب كانت في الجاهلية إذا فرغت من الحج

TABATABAI:2:198-200/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r5.claim: Here aw in “or more intensely” signals correction and means “rather.”
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r5.anchor: وأو في قوله أو أشد ذكرا للإضراب فتفيد معنى بل

TABATABAI:2:198-200/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r6.claim: Remembrance can be intense in quality as well as abundant in quantity.
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r6.anchor: وقد وصف الذكر بالشدة وهو أمر يقبل الشدة في الكيفية كما يقبل الكثرة في الكمية

TABATABAI:2:198-200/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r7.claim: Dhikr is not limited to spoken words: speech reports a presence of the heart.

TABATABAI:2:198-200/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r8.claim: The Qur’an illustrates abundant remembrance across circumstances with commands and descriptions of remembering God often, and remembering Him standing, sitting, and lying down.
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r8.anchor: الذين يذكرون الله قياما وقعودا وعلى جنوبهم

TABATABAI:2:198-200/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r9.claim: Because finishing pilgrimage invites distraction and forgetfulness of God, the verse fittingly calls for intense remembrance rather than simply abundant remembrance.

TABATABAI:2:198-200/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r10.claim: The division of people into those who seek worldly life and those who seek God’s approval follows from the command to remember Him.

TABATABAI:2:198-200/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r11.claim: “People” is generic: one group, including unbelievers, pursues worldly status and has no concern for the afterlife; the other seeks only what God approves, in either life, and has an afterlife share.
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r11.anchor: فالمراد به أفراد الإنسان أعم من الكافر

TABATABAI:2:198-200/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r12.claim: The verse’s “saying” and supplication describe an inward orientation or state, not necessarily literal spoken words.
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r12.anchor: وعلى هذا فالمراد بالقول والدعاء ما هو سؤال بلسان الحال دون المقال

TABATABAI:2:198-200/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r13.claim: The worldly seeker accepts whatever pleases his desire as good, while the seeker of God’s approval distinguishes good from evil in both lives and asks only for good.
TABATABAI:2:198-200/r13.anchor: لا يقيده بأن يكون حسنا عند الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:2:200-203/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:200-203/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:200-203/r1.claim: The contrast between having no afterlife share and receiving a share for one’s deeds shows that the first group’s works are nullified, unlike the second’s.
TABATABAI:2:200-203/r1.anchor: وما له في الآخرة من خلاق

TABATABAI:2:200-203/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:200-203/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:200-203/r3.claim: The passage urges remembrance: worldly-only seekers have no afterlife share, God-oriented seekers do, and God swiftly grants what His servant seeks; be among those with a share.

TABRISI:2:200/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:200/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:200/r1.claim: Qaḍāʾ fundamentally means deciding a matter firmly; it can mean finishing rites, completing an act, decisively announcing something, or issuing a binding judgment.
TABRISI:2:200/r1.anchor: أصل القضاء فصل الأمر على إحكام وقد يفصل بالفراغ منه كقضاء المناسك وقد يفصل بأن يعمل على تمام

TABRISI:2:200/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:200/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:200/r2.claim: Khalāq is an allotted share of good, originally a measure or entitlement; another derivation from khuluq makes it the share owed by noble character.
TABRISI:2:200/r2.anchor: والخلاق النصيب من الخير وأصله التقدير فهو النصيب من الخير على وجه الاستحقاق

TABRISI:2:200/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:200/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:200/r3.claim: أشد is genitive in agreement with the comparison, though it is indeclinable here because its form matches a verb and it is an adjective; it can also be accusative as a verbal noun, with ذكرا as specification.
TABRISI:2:200/r3.anchor: أشد في موضع جلا ولكنه لا ينصرف لأنه على وزن الفعل

TABRISI:2:200/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:200/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:200/r4.claim: في الآخرة may attach to the phrase governed by the lām in له; من خلاق is a subject with له as its predicate, and من is extra. Alternatively, في الآخرة is an adverbial circumstantial phrase.
TABRISI:2:200/r4.anchor: في الآخرة الجار والمجرور يتعلق بما يتعلق به اللام

TABRISI:2:200/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:200/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:200/r5.claim: The phrase means after performing or finishing the rites. Mansak can mean a place of worship, so the phrase covers completing what is due there, or a verbal noun pluralized because rites contain many acts and utterances.
TABRISI:2:200/r5.anchor: المناسك: جمع المنسك والمنسك يجوز أن يكون موضع النسك

TABRISI:2:200/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:200/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:200/r6.claim: One view takes the commanded remembrance as the takbīr specific to the days of Minā, the recommended remembrance of those days.
TABRISI:2:200/r6.anchor: أن المراد به التكبير المختص بأيام منى لأنه الذكر المرغب فيه المندوب إليه في هذه الأيام

TABRISI:2:200/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:200/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:200/r7.claim: A second view takes it as all supplications at those sacred stations, where prayer is better than elsewhere.
TABRISI:2:200/r7.anchor: أن المراد به سائر الأدعية في تلك المواطن لأن الدعاء فيها أفضل منه في غيرها

TABRISI:2:200/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:200/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
TABRISI:2:200/r8.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir reports that pilgrims used to gather after the rites to recount their ancestors' boasts, deeds, and past exploits; God directed them to remember Him instead.
TABRISI:2:200/r8.anchor: ما روي عن أبي جعفر الباقر ع أنهم كانوا إذا فرغوا من الحج يجتمعون هناك ويعدون مفاخر آبائهم ومآثرهم

TABRISI:2:200/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:200/r9.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:200/r9.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda say to remember God's favors even more, since His blessings exceed those of ancestors and He bestowed their virtues as well as ours; this explains comparison of the obligatory remembrance with a lesser one.
TABRISI:2:200/r9.anchor: على ذلك بأن يذكروا نعم الله ويعدوا آلاءه

TABRISI:2:200/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:200/r10.speaker: عطاء
TABRISI:2:200/r10.claim: ʿAṭāʾ instead says to seek help and refuge in God as a child turns to and repeatedly calls for its father; Tabrisi prefers the preceding explanation.
TABRISI:2:200/r10.anchor: وقيل معناه واستغيثوا بالله وافزعوا إليه كما يفزع الصبي إلى أبيه في جميع أموره

TABRISI:2:200/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:200/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:200/r11.claim: People at those sacred places fall into groups; one group asks only for worldly benefits and has no share of good in the afterlife because it does not believe in resurrection.
TABRISI:2:200/r11.anchor: بين سبحانه أن الناس في تلك المواطن أصناف فمنهم من يسأل نعيم الدنيا ولا يسأل نعيم الآخرة لأنه غير مؤمن بالبعث

TABRISI:2:200/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:200/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:200/r12.claim: In this context, no khalāq means no substantial or abundant share of good in the Hereafter.
TABRISI:2:200/r12.anchor: وما له في الآخرة من خلاق

FARRA:v1p121/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p121/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p121/r1.claim: Negated indefinite nouns may be split between nominative and accusative; this is poetic usage, not a canonical reading.
FARRA:v1p121/r1.anchor: وإن شئت رفعت بعض التبرئة ونصبت بعضا، وليس من قراءة القراء

FARRA:v1p121/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p121/r2.speaker: أمية
FARRA:v1p121/r2.claim: Umayya’s verse فلا لغو ولا تأثيم فيها illustrates mixed case after negation.
FARRA:v1p121/r2.anchor: قال أمية: فلا لغو ولا تأثيم فيها ... وما فاهوا به لهم مقيم

FARRA:v1p121/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p121/r3.speaker: الآخر
FARRA:v1p121/r3.claim: A second poet likewise mixes negated forms; the source also quotes the preceding line about who is called in hardship and when food is prepared.
FARRA:v1p121/r3.anchor: وقال الآخر : ذاكم- وجدكم- الصغار بعينه ... لا أم لي إن كان ذاك ولا أب

FARRA:v1p121/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p121/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p121/r4.claim: In pre-Islamic pilgrimage, people stood between the mosque at Minā and the mountain and praised their fathers’ deeds; the verse redirects them to remember God as much or more.
FARRA:v1p121/r4.anchor: كانت العرب إذا حجوا في جاهليتهم وقفوا بين المسجد بمنى وبين الجبل،

FARRA:v1p121/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p121/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p121/r5.claim: God answers that He is the one who performed those good deeds for them and their fathers.
FARRA:v1p121/r5.anchor: فأنزل الله تبارك وتعالى: «فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم أو أشد ذكرا»

FARRA:v1p121/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p121/r6.speaker: أهل الجاهلية
FARRA:v1p121/r6.claim: People of the pre-Islamic period asked for worldly wealth, camels, and sheep; خلاق means a share in the Hereafter.
FARRA:v1p121/r6.anchor: كان أهل الجاهلية يسألون المال والإبل والغنم فأنزل الله:

FARRA:v1p140/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p140/r1.speaker: أبو الجراح
FARRA:v1p140/r1.claim: In the verse he recited, كلاهما is nominative; أجد follows because the sense is “there is not one of the two that I do not find easy and comfortable.”
FARRA:v1p140/r1.anchor: أنشدني أبو الجراح: أرجزا تريد أم قريضا ... أم هكذا بينهما تعريضا

FARRA:v1p140/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p140/r2.speaker: الشاعر
FARRA:v1p140/r2.claim: An unattributed poem’s إلا وجدته construction shows an implicit negation in the sense “there is none of them except that I found him…”.
FARRA:v1p140/r2.anchor: قول الشاعر: فكلهم حاشاك إلا وجدته ... كعين الكذوب

THALABI:v2p114/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p114/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p114/r1.claim: The phrase means when you have finished Hajj and slaughtered the sacrificial rites.
THALABI:v2p114/r1.anchor: فإذا قضيتم مناسككم [فرغتم] من حجكم وذبحتم مناسككم

THALABI:v2p114/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p114/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p114/r2.claim: Nasaka describes slaughtering a sacrifice; mansak can mean the place of slaughter, by analogy with mashriq and maghrib.
THALABI:v2p114/r2.anchor: يقال منه نسك الرجل ينسك نسكا ونسكا ونسيكة ومنسكا إذا ذبح نسكه، والمنسك المذبح مثل المشرق والمغرب

THALABI:v2p114/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p114/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
THALABI:v2p114/r3.claim: Abu Amr assimilates the kaf into the following kaf here and in parallels throughout the Quran because the consonants are identical.
THALABI:v2p114/r3.anchor: وأبو عمرو يدغم الكاف في الكاف فيه وفي أخواته في كل القرآن مثل قوله ما سلككم لأنهما مثلان

THALABI:v2p114/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p114/r4.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v2p114/r4.claim: Most commentators say Arabs boasted of their fathers' achievements at the House after Hajj; God redirected them to remember Him for His favors to them and their fathers.
THALABI:v2p114/r4.anchor: قال أكثر المفسرين في هذه الآية: كانت العرب إذا فرغوا من حجهم وقفوا عند البيت وذكروا مآثر آبائهم ومفاخرهم

THALABI:v2p114/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p114/r5.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v2p114/r5.claim: Al-Suddi says men at Mina asked God for the wealth and status their fathers had, seeking worldly gifts rather than remembering God.
THALABI:v2p114/r5.anchor: قال السدي: كانت العرب إذا قضيت مناسكها وأقاموا بمنى يقوم الرجل فيسأل الله ويقول

THALABI:v2p114/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p114/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء والربيع والضحاك
THALABI:v2p114/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ata, al-Rabi, and al-Dahhak explain this as remembering God as small children eagerly speak of their parents.
THALABI:v2p114/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وعطاء والربيع والضحاك: معناه فاذكروا الله كذكر الصبيان الصغار الآباء

THALABI:v2p114/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p114/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p114/r7.claim: Asked why people may go a day without mentioning fathers, Ibn Abbas replied that God's anger at disobedience exceeds parents' anger when insulted.
THALABI:v2p114/r7.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: ليس كذلك ولكن من يغضب الله إذا عصى بأشد من غضبك لوالديك إذا أهنتهما

THALABI:v2p114/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p114/r8.speaker: القرظي
THALABI:v2p114/r8.claim: Al-Qurazi reads the comparison as remembering your fathers as they remember you.
THALABI:v2p114/r8.anchor: القرظي: في قوله فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم قال كذكركم آباءكم إياكم

THALABI:v2p114/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p114/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p114/r9.claim: Aw ashadda means even stronger, or rather more abundant in remembrance; the source compares Quranic phrases for greater hardness and fear.
THALABI:v2p114/r9.anchor: أو أشد ذكرا يعني أشد وبل أشد كقوله أو يزيدون مقاتل: أو أشد ذكرا أي أكثر ذكرا

THALABI:v2p114/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p114/r10.speaker: الأخفش
THALABI:v2p114/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash parses ashadda as accusative, supplying the sense: remember Him more intensely.
THALABI:v2p114/r10.anchor: وأما وجه انتصاب (أشد) ، فقال الأخفش: اذكروه أشد

THALABI:v2p115/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p115/r1.speaker: الزجاج
THALABI:v2p115/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj places ashadda in the genitive, though indeclinable as an adjective on the afʿal pattern, with dhikran as specification.
THALABI:v2p115/r1.anchor: وقال الزجاج: في محل الخفض لكنه لا ينصرف لأنه صفة على مفعال أفعل وصفته ذكرا على التمييز.

THALABI:v2p115/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p115/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p115/r2.claim: The worldly petitioner asks for camels, sheep, cattle, male servants, and female servants; the request's object is omitted.
THALABI:v2p115/r2.anchor: فمن الناس من يقول ربنا آتنا في الدنيا أي أعطنا إبلا وغنما وبقرا وعبيدا وإماء فحذف المفعول

THALABI:v2p115/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p115/r3.speaker: أنس
THALABI:v2p115/r3.claim: Anas says people circumambulated the House naked, praying for rain, victory over enemies, and a safe return to their people.
THALABI:v2p115/r3.anchor: قال أنس: كانوا يطوفون بالبيت عراة فيدعون ويقولون اللهم اسقنا المطر وأعطنا على عدونا الظفر

THALABI:v2p115/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p115/r4.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v2p115/r4.claim: Qatada describes a person whose sole aim is worldly life: he spends and works for it, and it is his concern, hope, and request.
THALABI:v2p115/r4.anchor: قتادة: هذا عبد نوى الدنيا لها أنفق ولها عمل ولها [قضت] فهي همه وأمنيته وطلبته

THALABI:v2p115/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p115/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p115/r5.claim: Khalaq means a share or portion in the Hereafter.
THALABI:v2p115/r5.anchor: وما له في الآخرة من خلاق حظ ونصيب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p48/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p48/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p48/r8.claim: Dhikr can mean remembering, as opposed to forgetting; the cited example is Moses’s companion saying Satan made him forget the fish.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p48/r8.anchor: فمما هو خلاف النسيان قوله: {وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان أن أذكره}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p48/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p48/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p48/r9.claim: Dhikr can also mean speech, whether speech that does not disparage its subject or speech that does; the latter is illustrated by a report about disparaging idols.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p48/r9.anchor: والذكر الذي هو قول يستعمل على ضربين: قول لا ثلب فيه للمذكور

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p48/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p48/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p48/r10.claim: ʿAdi ibn Hatim’s line uses yadhkurukum to mean disparage you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p48/r10.anchor: ومن ذلك قول الشاعر: يذكركم منا عدي بن حاتم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p48/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p48/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p48/r11.claim: Dhikra is also used as a verbal noun for remembering.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r1.claim: Here qaḍaytum means performed: one has qaḍā what was owed by carrying it out; completion is its underlying sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r1.anchor: وأراد هاهنا: أديتم، لأنه يقال: قضى ما عليه، إذا أداه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r2.claim: The phrase when prayer is concluded refers to Friday prayer and cannot mean making it up instead of performing it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r2.anchor: يعني: الجمعة، ولا يتصور فيها قضاء دون الأداء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r3.claim: Manāsik may be the plural of mansak as a verbal noun like nusk, meaning the worship commanded in Hajj.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r3.anchor: والمناسك: جمع منسك الذي هو مصدر، بمنزلة النسك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r4.claim: If manāsik is plural of a place of worship, the sense is completing the acts of the ritual places, with the annexed noun omitted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r4.anchor: وإن جعلتها جمع منسك الذي هو موضع العبادة، كان التقدير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r5.claim: Most exegetes say Arabs recalled their fathers’ deeds and boasts after Hajj, so God ordered them to remember Him, who favored them and their fathers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r5.anchor: قال أكثر أهل التفسير: كانت العرب إذا فرغوا من حجهم ذكروا مآثر آبائهم ومفاخرهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq says Arabs stood between the mosque at Mina and the mountain, listing their fathers’ virtues; God directs remembrance to monotheism and His blessings, since their fathers’ blessings came from God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: كانت العرب إذا قضت مناسكها وقفت بين المسجد بمنى وبين الجبل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r7.claim: In ʿAta’s narration, Ibn Abbas holds that remembrance redirects ancestral boasts to God’s oneness and blessings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r7.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس في رواية عطاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r8.speaker: الربيع والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r8.claim: Another report compares remembering God to remembering both parents; fathers alone suffice in the wording, as in the verse about clothing that protects from heat.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r8.anchor: والضحاك (¬5): أراد: فاذكروا الله كذكركم آباءكم وأمهاتكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r9.speaker: الربيع والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r9.claim: The authorities explain it as constantly mentioning the Lord in every state, like a young child who repeatedly says father and mother.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r9.anchor: أي: الهجوا بذكر ربكم في جميع أحوالكم، كما يلزم الصبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r10.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r10.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says Arabs commonly swore by their fathers, so God commands them to venerate Him as they venerated their fathers.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p57/r10.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري في هذه الآية: إن العرب كان أكثر أقسامها في الجاهلية بالآباء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p60/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p60/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p60/r1.claim: Aw ashadda dhikran means more strongly; its governor may be the kāf in ka-dhikrikum, putting it in genitive, or the verb udhkurū, putting it in accusative.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p60/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p60/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p60/r2.claim: The commanded remembrance is said to be takbir during the days at Mina, or supplication to God at those places.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p60/r2.anchor: وهذا الذكر المأمور به هو التكبير أيام منى، وقيل: إنه الدعاء لله عز وجل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p60/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p60/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p60/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies these people as polytheists asking for wealth, livestock, rain, victory, and worldly expansion, without an afterlife share because they disbelieved in it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p60/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هم المشركون، كانوا يسألون المال والإبل والغنم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p60/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p60/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p60/r4.claim: The object of ātinā is omitted because it is understood: they ask for what worldly life can provide.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p60/r4.anchor: وحذف مفعول {آتنا} من الكلام، وهو المسؤول من الدنيا؛ للعلم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p79#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p79#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p79#3/r1.claim: In pre-Islamic custom, pilgrims recalled their forefathers' finest deeds after completing the pilgrimage, such as hospitality and kinship ties.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p79#3/r1.anchor: كانوا في الجاهلية إذا فرغوا من حجهم ذكروا آباءهم بأحسن أفعالهم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p79#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p79#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p79#3/r2.claim: God commands remembrance equal to or greater than their remembrance of their fathers, since He did these good things for them and their fathers.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r2.claim: This means finishing the acts of worship commanded in the pilgrimage.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r2.anchor: أي: فرغتم من عباداتكم التي أمرتم بها في الحج

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r3.claim: After pilgrimage, Arabs used to recount their fathers’ boasts, so God commanded them instead to remember Him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r3.anchor: كانت العرب إذا فرغوا من حجهم ذكروا مفاخر آبائهم، فأمرهم الله عز وجل بذكره

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r4.claim: The phrase means to remember God even more intensely.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r4.anchor: أو أشد ذكرا } يعني: وأشد ذكرا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r5.claim: These people are polytheists who ask for wealth, camels, and sheep but no share in the afterlife, since they do not believe in it; Muslims ask for good in both worlds.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:199-200/r5.anchor: وهم المشركون كانوا يسألون المال والإبل والغنم، ولا يسألون

ELMALILI:2:200/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:200/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:200/r1.claim: Elmalılı explains manāsik here as the acts of worship connected with Hajj and locates the ensuing remembrance command in the days at Minā.
ELMALILI:2:200/r1.anchor: menâsikinizi, yani hacca müte‘allik ibadetlerinizi bitirdiğinizde

ELMALILI:2:200/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:200/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:200/r2.claim: Before Islam, Arabs stayed at Minā after Hajj between the mosque and mountain, recalling their ancestors' glories and notable days; this verse replaces that custom with remembrance of God.
ELMALILI:2:200/r2.anchor: Kable’l-İslâm Araplar âdetleri vechile menâsik-i haccı bitirdikten sonra Minâ’da mescid ile dağ arasındaki mevkide tevakkuf ederler

ELMALILI:2:200/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:200/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:200/r3.claim: The command sustains Hajj's sacred spiritual awakening; stoning the devil and saying takbir are its final, cherished reminders.
ELMALILI:2:200/r3.anchor: şeytan taşlamak ve tekbirler almak, bunun son bir hâtıra-i bergüzîdesidir.

ELMALILI:2:200/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:200/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:200/r4.claim: The Hajj rites enact the denial of association with God, making the practical implications of the declaration of divine unity visible.
ELMALILI:2:200/r4.anchor: kelime-i tevhiddeki nefy-i şirk mânası bütün levâzım-ı ameliyesiyle fiilen gösterilmiş oluyor.

ELMALILI:2:200/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:200/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:200/r5.claim: Hajj should lead beyond ancestral memory and personal, family, or tribal pride: its hardships and sacred history teach human frailty and the transience of the world before God's permanence.
ELMALILI:2:200/r5.anchor: fânîlerin aczlerini, bâkīnin sırr-ı bekāsını sezen âkil ü kâmil insanların bu ibadetten alacakları intibâh-ı rûhî

ELMALILI:2:200/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:200/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:200/r6.claim: The proper spiritual outcome is to cast off traces of shirk, pride, sensual drives, and false impressions, then live in prayer, repentance, dependence, and continual remembrance of God.
ELMALILI:2:200/r6.anchor: her türlü âsâr-ı şirki atıp vahdet-i külliyeye doğru yürümek nefsin gurûr-ı şahsî ve ailevî ve kavmîsini

ELMALILI:2:200/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:200/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:200/r7.claim: Some people ask only for worldly provision, with all their aspiration fixed on this life and no requested or expected share in the Hereafter.

ELMALILI:2:200/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:200/r8.speaker: İmam Fahreddin Râzî
ELMALILI:2:200/r8.claim: Rāzī classifies happiness as spiritual, bodily, and external; each has two forms: knowledge and virtue, health and beauty, wealth and status.
ELMALILI:2:200/r8.anchor: İmam Fahreddin Râzî tefsîrinde der ki: “Saadetlerin merâtibi üçtür: Rûhâniye

ELMALILI:2:200/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:200/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:200/r9.claim: A request for knowledge or virtue is worldly when sought for status or management of worldly affairs; those denying resurrection seek any virtue only for this life.
ELMALILI:2:200/r9.anchor: ilim dünyada tezeyyün ve akrâna tekaddüm için talep edilirse dünyadan olur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:200/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:200/r1.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:200/r1.claim: Reports say pre-Islamic Arabs delivered speeches after completing pilgrimage, sometimes seated in circles at Mina, praising their ancestors and competing in boasts about them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:200/r1.anchor: İslâm’dan önceki Araplar, haccı tamamladıktan sonra (bazı rivayetlerde Mina’da halkalar halinde oturup) atalarının büyüklüğü konusunda nutuklar çeker

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:200/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
